title: Word search
Greek Tzolis sustains thigh injury in match against Oranje
lead: Forward Christos Tzolis of the Greek national team sustained a thigh injury on Thursday in the home match against the Netherlands in the Nations League (2-2). The 24-year-old Arsenal player will therefore miss the meeting with Germany on Sunday in Thessaloniki. The Greek federation has announced this.

title: Cabinet changes budget again under pressure from Parliament: small savers are spared
lead: Minister <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) is open to a different lower threshold for the wealth tax in box 3 in order to spare the small saver. That is what the VVD minister said on the second day of the general financial considerations. "I had estimated that with the current threshold the small saver is spared, but <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> sees it differently."

title: Two lethal doses, but Christa Pike kept breathing: this is how the failed execution unfolded
lead: The execution of the American Christa Pike in Tennessee has failed. Pike was administered two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital, but kept breathing and snoring. What exactly happened? And where is Christa Pike now? This is what we know now.

title: Discontent in the House about box 3 now that small savers are 'the victims'
lead: The extra gestures by <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> have not yet produced the desired budget deal. Left-wing and right-wing opposition parties believe that workers pay too much tax. Parties also criticise that small savers "are the victims" of the new box 3 plan.

title: AI companies are lax on security. Should we ‘just accept that’, as Sam Altman says?
Why is the corner of a contestant's chair on 'De slimste mens' broken off?
Disagreement in coalition over approach to paper gifts: 'We should not do that'
lead: A majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> wants to partly pay for the reform of box 3 by tackling paper gifts. That is a fiscally favorable way to give money and pay less inheritance tax. But within the coalition there is disagreement about this: the VVD does not want that sacred cow of theirs to be touched. CDA and D66 are quite willing to look into this.

title: Cabinet does not want to cut social security, shifts to the right on box 3
lead: The cabinet plans to abandon the planned cuts to social security. With that it extends a hand to left-wing parties. Around the box 3 dossier, the cabinet actually wants to move to the 'right', sources confirm to NU.nl following reporting by De Telegraaf .

title: Many young hedgehogs are hit by cars: 'Unfortunately they cannot fly'
lead: For hedgehogs, the Dutch road is becoming increasingly dangerous. Every year more than 100,000 hedgehogs are killed by cars, while the species is already not doing well. NU.nl spoke with experts about the worrying development. "They cannot fly across the road, of course."

title: Christa Pike still alive after attempt to execute her, loud snoring heard
lead: The execution of Christa Pike in the prison in the American state of Tennessee has failed. The highest court of the United States decided yesterday that the execution of the 50-year-old woman could go ahead after all, after it had earlier been postponed. The woman has been taken to hospital.

title: National coach Xavi remorseful after poor first half by Oranje: 'This was my fault'
lead: National coach Xavi Hernández has apologised for the poor play by the Dutch national team in the away match against Greece (2-2) in the Nations League. "This was my fault. I take full responsibility for this."

title: AI and hospitality, do they go together? 'Guest contact is important but we also want to simplify the work'
lead: The hospitality industry faces challenges, such as staff shortages and high purchasing costs. Can AI offer a solution? And where is the limit of using AI in a sector that is based on hospitality and human contact?

title: How the tech elite intervenes in daily life
Damen wants billions from Germany after frigate order withdrawn
lead: Shipbuilder Damen is demanding almost 4.7 billion euros from Germany for the cancellation of the frigate order earlier this year. This is stated in a letter from the Dutch shipbuilder's lawyer, reports the German magazine Der Spiegel.

title: After his wife's death life no longer mattered to the lonely radio reporter, but football kept him on his feet
Man (34) shot dead in Amsterdam, police speak of targeted act
lead: In a shooting on the Amstelveenseweg in Amsterdam, a 34-year-old man from Amsterdam was killed last night. The police assume that it was a targeted act. "The shooter was after this man. He was not shot at by accident," says a spokesperson.

title: Verstappen wins first grand prix of this season in Malaysia
lead: Max Verstappen has finally secured his first victory of this season in Formula 1. The four-time world champion won in his Red Bull after a chaotic run-up in dominant fashion the Grand Prix of Bahrain, which was held in Malaysia.

title: D66 allays concerns about looming cuts to education
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to obtain up to 49 percent of the money needed for social security by making cuts to education. The cabinet has parked the billions in cuts to social security until there is a deal with the trade unions and employers. If that does not yield enough, the rest will be taken from other ministries. Coalition party D66 today allays concerns about those cuts. According to D66 MP Henk-Jan Oosterhuis, that is 'the very last thing you should do'.

title: Here in Suriname, (almost) everyone is forgiving of the royal family’s colonial past: ‘I don’t let that history bother me’
Belgian receives chemical castration after sexual offence, the Netherlands also has this
lead: A 21-year-old Belgian man has received a five-year suspended prison sentence, on the condition that he undergoes chemical castration. In the Netherlands too, libido-inhibiting medication is sometimes prescribed. "It is not a miracle cure."

title: House of Representatives wants Defence to be less dependent on American companies
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has the ambition to purchase at least 50 percent of military equipment in Europe from now on. But the trend is going in a different direction.

title: Man transfers nearly 3.9 million euros from company to himself, gets prison sentence
lead: A financial adviser who worked in Lemelerveld, in the <entity id="org:gemeente-dalfsen">gemeente Dalfsen</entity>, embezzled nearly 3.9 million euros from a company over a period of more than two years. He transferred the money in about seventy transactions to bank accounts over which he himself had control.

title: 7 October could well last until eternity
Maarten Heijmans and Xander Vrienten about their performance with roots music: 'America is astonishing, terrifying and super beautiful at the same time'
lead: Heijmans and Vrienten made a performance with American roots music. A journey along different faces of America. "You could say that the songs offer different answers to the question of how to live."

title: 'One of five arrested suspects at British air force base called emergency number himself'
lead: British media report that one of the five men arrested at the British air base RAF Fairford called the emergency number himself. Why he did that is not clear.

title: Europe taps diesel from emergency reserve after Trump threat: 'Problems back in a number of months'
lead: Europe will draw on emergency diesel reserves to push down high fuel prices. This happens after a threat from President Donald Trump. Is it a sensible choice? "If we do not solve the underlying problem, we will be back to square one in no time."

title: Coffee with Putin can cost you billions
lead: Today in Dagkoers: Putin asks oligarchs for a 'voluntary' contribution for the war, the prime minister of Spain has announced early elections and charging point providers stumble over expiring contracts amid the ever-increasing pressure on the power grid.

title: You can’t trade your way through the AI apocalypse
lead: It’s hard to price the threats posed by a misaligned superintelligence.

title: Gas treaty with Germany is a step back in the energy transition
Housing crisis? Cabinets want to decide without paying. But that is not how it works
lead: Yet another report concluding that the housing crisis would be helped by somewhat less political interference. <entity id="org:kabinet">Kabinet</entity> after cabinet ignores that advice, writes Marike Stellinga.

title: Portugal beats Denmark even without Ronaldo
lead: The Portugal footballers have recorded their third win in the Nations League against Denmark without star player Cristiano Ronaldo. In Copenhagen, the Portuguese won 4-2 after earlier victories over Wales and Norway.

lead: English football is gripped by a major scandal. Manchester City, enriched thanks to a sugar daddy from the United Arab Emirates, has the financial rules…

Feyenoord and PSV women's footballers to main tournament of Europa Cup
lead: The women footballers of Feyenoord and PSV have reached the main tournament of the Europa Cup, following Ajax. Feyenoord lost 2-1 at Norwegian Vålerenga, but had won the first match in Rotterdam 4-1. PSV successfully defended a 1-0 lead at Fortuna Hjørring. The match in Denmark ended 0-0.

title: Sjefietshe closes its doors, owner Bas Lammersen (42) wants to have his hands free for new things: 'I have a kind of seven-year itch'
VVD ministers on unrest among supporters about plans: 'I understand the fear'
lead: VVD voters have started thinking more negatively about the minority cabinet this week, according to research among VVD voters by the RTL Nieuwspanel. VVD government members reacted with understanding this morning at the start of <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. "I understand the fear among the supporters about the left-wing agenda," says VVD leader Dilan Yeşilgöz. "I think there have been better weeks," says minister <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> in response to the question whether it was a nice week for his party.

title: Lindsay Clancy case revolves around postpartum psychosis: Karin had to deal with it
lead: It is a murder case that is causing quite a stir in the US: the Lindsay Clancy case. The 36-year-old woman killed her three children. She herself says that the act cannot be held against her, because at that moment she was suffering from a severe postpartum psychosis. Whether that is the truth still has to be seen. But that it can be intense is a fact, Karin den Oudsten knows from experience.

title: Stolen data of customers of grocery service Flink offered for sale by criminals
lead: The stolen private data of customers of grocery service Flink is being offered for sale by cybercriminals: the highest bidder may have the data. The criminals claim to have stolen the data of a million customers and more than 10,000 employees.

title: Van Weel calls extortion site 'terrible', asks police to support Belgian colleagues
lead: Minister of Justice <entity id="person:david-van-weel">David van Weel</entity> calls the extortion site with nude images of Dutch and Belgian women 'terrible'. "I will also ask the Dutch police to possibly help the Antwerp police with this," Van Weel said during the Question Hour in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Assassination attempt Overasselt prepared in app groups: 'I need boys. 10K per man'
lead: The group of suspects that was on a murder mission in Overasselt discussed the attack in advance in hundreds of messages on Signal and Snapchat. This is evident from a reconstruction by RTL Nieuws based on the criminal file. Several contract killers appear to have been recruited online.

lead: In the coming days a high-pressure area will provide calm and dry weather. This morning there is a regional chance of fog. As soon as it has disappeared, the sun will come out well. The afternoon temperature remains at a pleasant level for the beginning of October.

title: Deadline for custom agreements on making Tata more sustainable postponed
lead: The <entity id="org:provincie-noord-holland">provincie Noord-Holland</entity> wants to make 'clear agreements' about making Tata Steel more sustainable, but more time is needed for that. The province, the national government and the steel company agreed last year to do this before 30 September 2026. However, that deadline is being pushed back by six months, to 1 March 2027.

title: American soldier arrested for murder of Japanese woman, and so a decades-long debate erupts again
De Bruyne guides Belgium past Turkey in Nations League: 3-0
lead: The Belgian national football team defeated Turkey 3-0 in Liege in the Nations League. Kevin De Bruyne scored two goals at Stade Maurice Dufrasne (Sclessin) for the team of national coach Mark van Bommel. Romelu Lukaku took the third goal for his account.

title: 'Hand in your phone and wallet', said the man in the metro
lead: In the metro in which Marcel van Roosmalen and his daughter (11) were sitting, a man shouted that everyone had five minutes to hand in their phone and wallet to him. The people looked the other way and pretended it was not happening. My daughter had accidentally made eye contact and could not stop doing so because she thought he was now keeping an eye on us.

We moeten ophouden met liegen over liegen
Verstappen drives second time in third practice Sepang
lead: Max Verstappen drove the second time in the third free practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The four-time world champion in Formula 1 was slightly less fast at the Sepang circuit than Kimi Antonelli. The Dutchman conceded 0.278 seconds in his Red Bull to the Italian championship leader in his Mercedes.

title: De Librije in Zwolle remains the only three-star restaurant in the Netherlands
lead: De Librije was awarded three stars for the twenty-third time on Monday in Maastricht during Michelin's annual ceremony. It is the only restaurant with that status. The Netherlands has gained two two-star restaurants: Azurite in Delft and Suis in Schin op Geul.

title: What will you notice from the cabinet plans?
Collision in Amstelveen ends in bystander being threatened with firearm
Hole in ship Eemshaven sealed, danger averted
lead: Near the Eemshaven in Groningen a ship got into serious trouble last night. It concerns the ship the 'Nautilus'. It threatened to capsize for a moment, but because a lot of water was pumped out and the hole in the hull has been sealed, the situation is now under control, says a spokesperson for the Groningen safety region. The ship is 73 by 16 metres.

title: PRO will not yet support tax plan: not social enough
lead: PRO is not yet enthusiastic about the plans for taxes for 2027. MP Luc Stultiens criticises that extra money is mainly being raised from workers, but not from large fortunes. "It is not social enough."

title: Sourness at the VVD now that the left crows victory over the budget
lead: Sourness within the VVD. PRO leader Jesse Klaver rejoices on social media that he won the Prinsjesdag negotiations. Not the liberals. Local VVD administrators are being held to account. And grumble.

title: Governance crisis in the province of Gelderland with BBB over nitrogen rules averted
Dumfries wants to give Van Dijk victory as gift for 100th international match
lead: The Dutch national team wants to give captain Virgil van Dijk a victory as a gift for his hundredth international match on Sunday in the home match against Serbia in the Nations League. That is what right wing-back Denzel Dumfries said, who himself begins his eightieth match for the Dutch national team on Sunday.

title: Skincare in the children's room: cosmetics giants push their unnecessary products on kids via TikTok
lead: From TikTok videos to workshops at the drugstore: skincare has long ceased to be only for adults. Cosmetics brands have discovered a young target group. Experts warn about the effect that skincare products can have on children.

title: Municipalities want to be able to exclude foreign hardware in procurement
lead: Dutch municipalities want to be able to exclude foreign technology in their new joint purchase of laptops, smartphones and other workplace hardware if cybersecurity or national security interests require it. Future 'Made in Europe' rules will also already get a place in the procurement. With this, the <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">VNG</entity> is emphatically responding in the new hardware contracts to the growing call for more digital autonomy.

title: Fury wants to invite Trump to attend boxing match with Joshua
lead: CARDIFF (ANP/AFP) - British boxer Tyson Fury (36) wants to walk into the ring together with US President Donald Trump for the long-awaited fight with his compatriot Anthony Joshua (38). The fight between the two British former heavyweight world champions is scheduled for 11 December in Cardiff.

title: Schaduwen van de Oranjezon: an end to the Orange-minded colonial fairy tale?
lead: A portrait of the queen who kindly watches over the class above the school blackboard, or orange flags during a visit by the royal family to the Antilles: the prevailing image of the view of the Oranjes in the former colonies is sunny: royalism everywhere and the friendliest mutual relations. But in Schaduwen van de Oranjezon that image is being shaken. The book is one of the five that appear as the result of the large-scale investigation into the role of the royal house in colonial history, which was carried out at the expense and initiative of the royal house. Compilers Esther Captain, historian and member of the research committee, and professor of history Guno Jones talk about this in OVT.

title: Suriname misses out on Nations League continuation after dramatic ending, Vaessen comes to blows
lead: In the night from Monday to Tuesday (Dutch time), Suriname dramatically missed out on a place in the final round of the Nations League. The team of national coach Henk Fraser lost due to a goal in extra time and missed the quarter-finals on goal difference.

title: 'Reading now helps me to better understand my own world'
lead: Classics teacher Ninah Tiemersma (29) uses stories from Greek and Roman antiquity to help students think about emotions, resilience and personal development. She recently reread Van de koele meren des doods by Frederik van Eeden.

title: Nieuwe Red Line-protest gepland voor november
lead: Over iets meer dan een maand, op 8 november, vindt er weer een Red Line-protest plaats in Nederland.

title: Verdachte van moord op gevangenisbewaker bij NDSM in Amsterdam nog 90 dagen vast
lead: De rechter-commissaris heeft de 37-jarige Amin D. nog 90 dagen in bewaring gesteld, bevestigde een woordvoerder van de rechtbank aan NL Times.

title: It is impossible to keep a child away from a death
UEFA investigates alleged spitting incident during charged match between Ireland and Israel
lead: UEFA is going to investigate an alleged spitting incident during the Nations League match between Ireland and Israel last Sunday. A spokesperson for the European football association confirmed this to the ANP on Tuesday.

title: Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution
lead: Christa Pike, whose execution failed after two attempts, is according to her lawyer unconscious and on a ventilator. According to the lawyer she is intubated, meaning her breathing is regulated via an inserted airway tube. The doctors would be trying to save her life.

title: Total student debt falls for the first time
lead: The total student debt of students and former students was 3% lower at the start of this year, at €28 bn. In recent decades it increased every year.

title: Calm, dry and warm autumn weather: 'We will hold on to this for a little while'
lead: It will remain calm, dry and fairly warm for a few more days. At night and in the morning there is a chance of fog. From Thursday the weather will change, according to the expectation.

title: Will the war in Ukraine stop soon?
lead: The war in Ukraine is a war of attrition. The warring countries try to damage each other so much until one gives up. Russia's demands currently focus on capitulation of the Donetsk province and renouncing NATO membership. Ukraine, which for years claimed victory, is asking for an immediate ceasefire. Does a negotiated end also stand a chance? […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Drinking water companies must be the first to pay attention to data centre consumption, says minister
lead: ‘The supply agreement between a drinking water company and a business customer is a private-law agreement and does not form part of the permit granting process.’ That is what minister <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Vincent Karremans</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> writes in response to parliamentary questions about the 1.1 billion litres of drinking water per year that two new data centres in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>-Zuidoost will consume.

title: Underpants handed out to women at Oktoberfest after filming under skirts
lead: Visitors to a popular attraction at the Oktoberfest in Munich who wear a skirt or dress can get free underpants at the entrance. That must counter so-called 'upskirting', secretly filming under skirts. The regional German broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk (BR) discovered that thousands of euros are earned with this kind of video.

title: During the day of protest in Paris everyone feels: this is a decisive moment. 'It is now about more than the schools'
Dozens injured in major fire at campsite with many Dutch people on Lake Garda
lead: At a campsite on the southern shore of Lake Garda, at least 24 people were injured in a major fire. They all had to be taken to hospital. According to Italian media, one of them is said to be in critical condition. The campsite is popular with Dutch people.

title: Belgian receives Nobel Prize in Physics for study of mysterious particles in the universe
lead: The Belgian scientist Francis Halzen receives the Nobel Prize in Physics. He is the founder of the measurement of neutrinos. These are mysterious particles with extremely high energy that are produced in the universe.

title: The Jetten cabinet will have a hard time in the Senate, but Pro and VVD do find each other there
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> defended his plans on Tuesday in a sceptical Senate. It will still be difficult to steer all budgets through the senate. Parties make many demands, "then we also get to have a party once".

title: In Carré, rock band De Staat lets the audience feel how mass manipulation works
lead: All the ingredients were present on Friday for an impressive, even threatening experience in theater Carré in Amsterdam. Yet the performance by De Staat did not entirely convince. Precisely with doomsday images, you expect a more consistent dramaturgical track.

title: Dumfries and Xavi want to return to shorter international periods
lead: Defender Denzel Dumfries and national coach Xavi Hernández do not consider UEFA's experiment with a long international period containing four matches in a week and a half to be a success. Both said so on Saturday in Zeist, where they looked ahead during a press conference to Sunday's meeting with Serbia in the Nations League.

title: Council of State gives Noord-Brabant new deadline on poultry farmers
lead: The province of Noord-Brabant must make a final decision by 4 February 2027 at the latest on whether or not to withdraw the nature permits of five poultry farmers. The Council of State has ruled this. If the province misses the deadline, it must pay a penalty.

title: Lionel Messi crying in the team bus heading to the stadium, Argentine fans are already making a spectacle of it
lead: Lionel Messi plays against Benin (kick-off at 01:00) his 208th and final international match for Argentina. It promises to be a grand spectacle at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, where 85,000 fans can sing to the 39-year-old star player one last time. Follow our live blog of the match and all the Messi madness here.

title: Portugal's Leão wears Ronaldo's number 7 against Denmark
lead: Portuguese footballer Rafael Leão has been given shirt number 7 for Thursday's Nations League match against Denmark. This is shown by the squad list published by UEFA. Number 7 has belonged to Ronaldo for the past decades. Portugal's record international left the training camp on Wednesday amid discord. He played 234 internationals for his country.

title: Two dead in major accident with cars and trucks on N48 near Zuidwolde
lead: In a collision on the N48 near Zuidwolde in Drenthe, two truck drivers were killed. Three trucks and three cars were involved in the accident, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> confirms. The road is closed in both directions until the morning.

title: With this clothing doctors can safely treat an Ebola patient
lead: A care worker infected with the Ebola virus is being cared for at the LUMC. To make sure the virus cannot spread, the doctors and nurse follow an extensive dressing procedure.

title: BMX rider Laura Smulders wins World Cup race in China
lead: BMX rider Laura Smulders has won the fifth World Cup race of the season. The European champion was the best in the final in the Chinese Mentougou. It is the thirtieth World Cup victory of the 32-year-old from Nijmegen.

title: More than 250,000 French school pupils out for 'mass actions' on national protest day
lead: Boarded-up shops, confrontations with officers and blocked schools: on Tuesday another national protest day of French school pupils takes place. There are already more than 260,000 demonstrators out, reports the French trade union.

title: Oranje to Greece without injured Van Hecke
lead: The Dutch national team departed for Thessaloniki on Wednesday without Jan Paul van Hecke for Thursday's away match against Greece in the Nations League. The defender picked up an injury at the last training session in Zeist and is returning to his club Tottenham Hotspur, reports the KNVB.

title: Replica VOC ship Batavia gets a new spot in Lelystad
lead: The Batavia, a replica of a 17th-century VOC ship, will be placed on land after 31 years at the quay. The ship gets a new spot at Museum Batavialand in Lelystad and will be preserved there for the future.

title: Amsterdam asks minister for plan for treating crack addicts
lead: Amsterdam asks minister <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Sophie Hermans</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity> to quickly provide clarity about the halting of a study into a medicine for people with a severe crack or cocaine addiction. Mayor <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Femke Halsema</entity> and alderman Alexander Scholtes of Zorg write in a letter that they want Hermans to bring the parties involved together before 1 November to look for a solution.

title: Zoë Papaikonomou (44) rewrites news headlines: 'It is not an asylum crisis, but a shelter scandal'
Paulien Cornelisse was no schoolmaster, her pleasure in language was the key to her success
'Before Flydubai flight departed, UAE authorities shared list of passengers and crew members with Israel'
lead: Before the Flydubai flight flew to Tel Aviv last week, authorities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) shared the lists of passengers and crew members with Israel. That is reported by regional officials. During the flight the co-pilot attacked the commander of the aircraft, in an attempt to make the plane crash.

title: Even a fall is complicated with this minority cabinet
lead: New elections could be a long way off. Because when does a minority cabinet actually fall? Political traumas from the past are hindering the <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten, but at the same time stand in the way of a breakthrough. Political reporter Hans van Soest writes weekly about Hague affairs that affect us all.

title: Drone images show devastation after floods in Spain
lead: In the southeast of Spain, heavy rain showers caused significant flooding. A 102-year-old woman died in the process.

title: British bestselling author and former politician Jeffrey Archer (86) died
lead: The British author and former politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86. Archer sold hundreds of millions of books and was a member of parliament for the Conservative Party, but also spent two years in prison for perjury.

title: Maybe I can buy the fatbike from him and then throw it in the canal
Oranje fails to keep a clean sheet against the Greeks for the eleventh match in a row
lead: The Dutch national team has not yet managed to finish a single match without conceding this calendar year. In the Nations League match against Greece on Thursday, Oranje conceded at least one goal for the eleventh match in a row.

title: Colleagues on the loss of their friend Paulien Cornelisse. 'She was sharp, but without hurting anyone'
Argument over billions bill: box 3 tax remains a divisive issue in the coalition
Griekspoor out in first round of China Open against Russian Rublev
lead: Tallon Griekspoor has been eliminated in the first round of the China Open. The 30-year-old tennis player lost in Beijing in three sets to the Russian Andrey Rublev: 4-6 7-5 6-7 (6). Rublev now faces his compatriot Roman Safiullin.

title: Man without driving licence and under the influence collides with ambulance in Rotterdam
lead: In Rotterdam, a car collided with an ambulance this evening. The ambulance was on the Prins Alexanderlaan this evening with blaring sirens transporting a patient to the hospital when things went wrong. The driver of the car turned out to be under the influence and did not have a driving licence.

title: Images of Russian drone hitting bridge in Kyiv
lead: There are images of the moment a Russian drone hits a bridge in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv. That happens while a lot of traffic is driving over the bridge.

title: Website does not deliver food to your home, but does give a dopamine kick
lead: The mere prospect of a meal can provide a small dopamine kick. And these days you do not even have to spend money on it. On the website FoodNeverComes you order for fun: you choose a dish, put it in your shopping cart, pay, receive a confirmation and even a reminder that your order is on its way. Only in the end nothing arrives - except perhaps a little dopamine.

title: Podcast | The cabinet's new 'offer': 'VVD seems to have given up'
lead: The cabinet suddenly came with a new 'offer' to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> to still strike a deal on the budget. But besides joy, there was irritation about the details of the plans.

title: Vollering solos to second consecutive European Championship gold a week after world title
lead: Cyclist Demi Vollering has become European road champion for the second year in a row. The brand-new world champion rode away on the final climb of the Možjanca in sunny Slovenia and soloed the last 15 kilometres to the finish in Šenčur. Fellow countrywoman Puck Pieterse won the sprint for silver from the chasing group, ahead of the Swiss Marlen Reusser.

title: Mark Boumans new chairman of gymnastics association
lead: Mark Boumans has been appointed chairman of the Koninklijke Nederlandse Gymnastiek Unie (KNGU). He takes office on 1 November, the association reports in a press release. Boumans will soon stop as <entity id="pos:burgemeester-doetinchem">burgemeester van Doetinchem</entity>.

title: Frank van der Linde collected 500,000 from the government: 'Can you justify investing so much in the repression of a peaceful activist?'

Misleading humour is an effective political weapon
lead: Misleading humour is an effective political weapon, says Beer Prakken. He obtained his PhD for his research into humour in political debate. 'Someone like Trump mobilises and radicalises his following with humour and ambiguity.' And how does that work here?

title: American court case with AI victim statement must be redone
lead: An American court case in which an AI video was shown in the courtroom as a victim statement must be redone. The court in Arizona has ruled that the video was 'not reliable', which means the sentence is considered unfair.

title: Five questions about box 3: how could it become such a problem and what is the solution now?
lead: The new coalition plan for the tax on wealth (box 3) will be the most important subject during the Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen, which take place in the coming two days. The question is whether an end will come to this headache file, which has occupied politics for years. What is box 3 and how could it become such a problem? The most important questions in a row. Box 3: what falls under it again? Do you have little savings, no investments and do you not have a second home? Then you will presumably have nothing at all to do with box 3. In that case you pay, like most Dutch people, only tax in box 1 on your wages or benefit. This box yields by far the most for the treasury: around 90 percent of all income tax. Box 2 is intended for people with a business, such as a private limited company. This is estimated at 500,000 people. In box 3 there are around 2.5 million people. In it you pay tax on returns on savings, shares, cryptocurrencies and also a second home. Why must box 3 be overhauled? Politics could do no other after a ruling by the <entity id="org:hoge-raad">Hoge Raad</entity> in 2021 . It ruled that the estimated return with which the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> calculated was not fair. Savers in particular were the victims of this: they often paid more tax than they received in interest from the bank. To comply with the court ruling, the <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Rutte III quickly set up a temporary way of calculating tax, which still applies to this day. But this system also has a major disadvantage: people with high returns now pay relatively little tax. As a result, the treasury receives 3 billion euros less annually than before. Every year that no new plan comes, those billions 'leak' away. For that reason political parties feel time pressure to quickly come up with an alternative. Work was done on this in the Rutte IV, Schoof and Jetten cabinets. Debate about Box 3 The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> debates today with <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) about the budget and Box 3. That debate can be followed live from 10.30 am via a livestream on NOS.nl and in the NOS app. On which plan was work being done? For this, the difference between wealth accretion tax and wealth gain tax is important: - With a wealth accretion tax you must pay every year on the profit you make, even if that profit is still 'locked up' in for example shares. So it can be that if you have no savings, you must sell (part of) the shares or crypto to be able to pay your tax. - With wealth gain tax you pay tax on the shares or cryptocurrencies that you have sold. Disadvantage of that method is that owners can postpone the sale to avoid tax. The coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA agree that in the long term a wealth gain tax must come. But there is a technical problem: according to the Ministry of Finance this is only possible from 2030 or even 2032, because the Belastingdienst and banks must adjust their systems for this. Politics debated in recent years about the question of what should happen in the meantime. The Tweede Kamer (including D66, VVD and CDA) agreed at the beginning of this year to a new, temporary solution to introduce a wealth accretion tax on shares and cryptocurrencies from 2028 and a wealth gain tax on real estate. After that, work would be done towards a full wealth gain tax. This interim solution led to so much unrest among companies and investors , that minister Heinen (Financiën, VVD) said two weeks later that the law had to go back to the drawing board. Subsequently a major difference of opinion arose between coalition parties about what should then happen. What did they disagree about? The VVD wants to switch to a full wealth gain tax as quickly as possible, even though the Belastingdienst will then temporarily be less able to check returns properly because the systems have not yet been adjusted for it. The biggest problem is that the treasury will then receive an estimated more than 15 billion euros less in the coming years. That is because people only start paying tax when they sell their shares. The parties mainly disagreed about the question of who should pay for that. D66 and CDA did not want lower incomes to contribute to this. What is the solution now? The cabinet now wants to switch to a wealth gain tax for shares, bonds and second homes as of 2028, the rest follows in 2030. The funding is sought in box 2 and box 3 . Of that, the proposal around the tax-free income in box 3 is politically the most sensitive. In the new box 3 there will no longer be tax-free wealth (which is now 59,357 euros for one person), but a tax-free income. The idea is that people with high returns also pay more tax. In the original plan you start paying tax with an annual return above 1800 euros. In the new plan that has been lowered to 1000 euros. As a result, hundreds of thousands of small investors would soon also have to pay tax on their profit from shares. JA21 and SGP have already said that that part of the funding is "unacceptable". They say that the cabinet has promised them to come up with another solution. So possibly a line will again be drawn through this part of the plan. The situation around box 3 is now fairly chaotic. Because the Tweede Kamer has already agreed to the wealth accretion in box 3 law, it is now with <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. If the cabinet has a majority for the new plan, it must go through the Tweede Kamer again via a legislative amendment (novelle). Only after that can the Eerste Kamer vote on it.

title: New OM guideline: higher sentencing demands for violence against emergency workers
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> must from now on always bring cases involving violence against people with a public function before the court. In doing so, the prosecution service must also always demand a sentence twice as heavy, with imprisonment as the starting point. This is stated in a new guideline from the College van procureurs-generaal, the national leadership of the Openbaar Ministerie, which takes effect tomorrow. Justice Minister Van Weel writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> that this guideline will apply not only to police officers and emergency workers, but also, for example, to teachers who face violence. The minister gives as an example an attempted aggravated assault on an emergency worker, in which the perpetrator does not use a weapon, has not previously offended, and the emergency worker has not been injured. The sentencing demand would then in principle be three months in prison, instead of 80 hours of community service if the victim had not been an emergency worker. Heavier punishment already possible The new guideline is a concession to the Tweede Kamer. Early this year, shortly before the swearing-in of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten, it argued for demanding heavier sentences for violence against emergency workers. The Kamer expressed its horror at the increasing violence against police officers and emergency workers after it had gotten completely out of hand again a few weeks earlier during the New Year's period. Since 2006, people who are aggressive and violent toward people with a public task can already be punished 200 percent more heavily than other violent offenders. But according to the Kamer, the OM does too little with this, so that perpetrators can still get away with community service or a fine. In particular, right-wing parties in the Tweede Kamer have asked in motions for heavier sentences for violence against emergency workers. "I fully endorse that line," the minister of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> writes today in his letter. Banning community service Van Weel considers it "unacceptable" that public prosecutors would not follow earlier standards on heavier sentences, because "violence and aggression against people with a public task is inadmissible". "Society cannot do without the police officer, the healthcare worker, the teacher and all other persons with a public task," he states. "They keep our society running and must be able to do their work safely and without hindrance." There is still a proposal from the Tweede Kamer to ban community service entirely for violence against emergency workers. Last year, that drew criticism from the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> and judges, who want to retain the room to judge independently and to be able to weigh specific circumstances.

title: House of Representatives wants to get rid of tax for small investors and savers
lead: In the House of Representatives there is little enthusiasm for the plan to start taxing hundreds of thousands of small investors and savers . JA21, ChristenUnie and SGP are not keen on it, and Pro is also principled against it. That makes a parliamentary majority for the plan seem out of sight. "It is a fine on thrift or successful entrepreneurship," says SGP MP Flach during the General Financial Considerations. "Disastrous for the ambition to get more Dutch people to invest their savings," thinks JA21 MP Hoogeveen. After a barrage of questions to coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA, they said they were willing to look at other solutions. "We too find this an unfortunate point," said CDA MP Van Dijk. What exactly is in box 1, 2 and 3 and what is now the solution that has been proposed for box 3? You can read that in this article: Many parties are nevertheless positive that the coalition wants to introduce a capital gains tax on shares, bonds and second homes from 2028, and also on cryptocurrencies from 2030. That would finally provide a solution to the political problem around box 3 after years of discussion. 'Take 200 euros, give back 100 euros' The opposition was more critical of the billions that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> wants to raise next year by increasing income tax. Although the cabinet says work must pay, the opposite is happening, the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> noted earlier. Yet VVD MP Van Eijk does not intend to strike this plan. She points out that the purchasing power of many people is still improving . Opposition parties reacted critically. "That is first take 200 euros, give back 100 euros and then you have to be happy," said for example BBB-<entity id="person:hendrik-vermeer">Kamerlid Vermeer</entity>. How the coalition wants to get a majority for the Tax Plan therefore remains unclear. JA21 and Pro also want to support the cabinet only if the increased income tax is scaled back. Soothe concerns For left-wing parties the morning started festively: they congratulated each other that the cuts to social security are off the table after strikes . Because Pro wants to support the budget of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity> as a result, there now seems to be a majority for this budget. Yet there were also many questions because of the table that <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) circulated, after it leaked yesterday via the NOS . It shows that a large part of the amount that is no longer being cut from social security is now provisionally placed on the education budget. D66, which profiles itself as an education party, tried to soothe the concerns about this among the left-wing parties. MP Oosterhuis (D66) spoke of a table written by an "overzealous civil servant", which was "not so relevant" and "without political value". But from Van Eijk (VVD) a different sound was heard. She confirms that it is "the technical elaboration" of the agreement within the coalition that if the cut to social security does not succeed, cuts will be made to education. Asked whether that is a sensible choice, she answers that more money "has not necessarily led to qualitatively better education". The coalition said yesterday that it expects the reforms of social security to still lead to savings. If an amount then remains, the parties want to sit down next year to see where that money should then come from. Starting signal for further negotiations Tomorrow is the second day of the General Financial Considerations. Then minister Heinen (Financiën) and <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (Fiscaliteit) will respond to the questions from the House of Representatives. It will be the starting signal for further negotiations. The uncertainty about the cabinet's financial plans will therefore remain for a while. That may change towards the handling of the Tax Plan, which the House of Representatives will start discussing from mid-October. In it, it is agreed how the government will collect taxes in the coming years.

title: Government takes over supervision of estate agents from estate agents themselves
lead: With fresh reluctance, housing minister Boekholt-O'Sullivan (D66) is going to involve herself in the estate agency sector. She is going to introduce an estate agents register and a complaints desk for dissatisfied buyers and sellers. "Very many people have the feeling that it is not a fair process to buy or sell a house." The minister had research done. Nearly a third of the respondents had at least one negative experience with an estate agent, in many cases a selling agent. Nearly ninety percent of the complaints were about an estate agent affiliated with a trade association. Only two percent of those people filed an official report. The minister would have preferred that the sector itself had reached agreements on quality and fairness. The professional organisations together represent a large part of the market and would normally have to have a lot of influence on implementing improvements, the minister thought. But in conversations with the various estate agents' organisations, they told her that despite codes of conduct and improvement plans they had not succeeded. They think they are not strong enough against rogue estate agents. So the government has to step in. "That is a big step and so I would rather not have done it," says Boekholt. In the government's estate agents register, all estate agents will have to register in order to be allowed to practise their profession. "With that you conform to certain rules. You work transparently, you are honest and you show the bidding book." A bidding log is a record of all bids that have been made on a home. "Sometimes people get advice from their estate agent to bid ten thousand euros more," says Boekholt. "But they have no idea whether there is a bid from other people underneath." Some estate agents drive up the price that way. Or they favour certain clients. Or they disadvantage their client by passing on confidential information. Boekholt emphasises that most estate agents work normally and assist their clients well. It concerns a small number that misbehaves. For clients who encounter that, there will be a disputes committee. Depending on the severity of the complaints or the number of complaints, it can in the extreme case expel an estate agent and remove them from the register. They can then no longer practise their profession in the Netherlands. Estate agent is a free profession Since 2001, anyone who wants to can call themselves an estate agent. No legally required diploma is needed. You can join a trade association, but that is not necessary. There are now two trade associations: NVM and Vastgoed Nederland. They have drawn up rules, but those are not strictly enforced. The trade associations say that estate agents will then deregister. Complaints about estate agents are not a new phenomenon and there are many of them. Vereniging Eigen Huis (VEH) reported in August that since February more than 900 complaints about estate agents had come in to the reporting desk. The PVV in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> is coming with a bill for the estate agency sector because of the persistent complaints. MP Mooiman proposes rules of conduct, a national professional register, external supervision and fines for violations. The sector organisations responded positively to this. <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">Minister Boekholt</entity> sees Mooiman's bill as help on the way to effective and enforceable legislation. "That is why I am happy to join forces with the submitter." At the beginning of 2027, concrete proposals will be on the table, the minister promises.

title: Self-employed act must give self-employed workers and clients clarity
lead: After years of discussion about false self-employment, a new law must put an end to the discussion about when someone is a self-employed worker and when not. "This must provide clarity for entrepreneurs and clients," says <entity id="person:thierry-aartsen">minister Aartsen</entity> of Werk en Participatie. Clients who work with false self-employed workers run the risk of additional assessments from the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> for tax and social contributions. Because of the unclear rules, some clients therefore stopped hiring self-employed workers. The new law contains criteria that self-employed workers and clients can hold on to, Aartsen says. If you work independently of others, bear entrepreneurial risks and have the freedom to organise your work yourself, then you are an entrepreneur. Three clients Concretely, it means that you must be registered with the <entity id="org:zbo-kamer-van-koophandel">Kamer van Koophandel</entity>, have a VAT number, a business bank account and issue invoices and make business payments. Calculated over two years, you must have at least three different clients or customers and be active in acquiring new clients. "These are not unreasonable criteria that we set," Aartsen says. "If you meet them, you can be sure that you do not need to fear additional assessments." The work itself must also meet criteria. As an entrepreneur, you must in principle be free to determine where, when and how you carry out the assignment. Unless the work really can only be carried out at a certain location such as a construction site, or at a certain time such as repair work outside office hours or opening hours. Pension and insurance Furthermore, the self-employed worker must make provisions that an employee in salaried employment does not need. Insurance against illness and incapacity for work, pension, insurance for damage caused by the work and other entrepreneurial risks. A minimum amount for this will be included in the law; you do not need to have all those provisions. "We want to discuss with entrepreneurs the amount that a self-employed worker must spend at least on these provisions," Aartsen says. "It must not be too much, but it must also not become an empty shell." For most entrepreneurs, all of this is self-evident. They are legally recognised as independent entrepreneurs by this law. But precisely for the group where it is not clear, the law must help them to still meet the criteria. Until 29 October, interested parties can respond to the legislative texts via Internetconsultatie.nl . After that, there will still be debates with the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. The law will not enter into force earlier than 1 January 2028.

title: Bolle Jos now also on the agenda in Europe: payments to Sierra Leone halted
lead: The European Commission has immediately halted payments to Sierra Leone because the country is not cooperating with the extradition of drug criminal Bolle Jos. That is confirmed by <entity id="person:david-van-weel">minister Van Weel</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> after a report in De Telegraaf. Sierra Leone would still receive 18 million euros in budget support from Brussels this year. That money is intended for, for example, food programmes, education and infrastructure in the impoverished country. The Netherlands hopes that next year a payment of another 22.5 million can be halted. That is still being negotiated between the EU member states. Turning off the money tap is a long-cherished wish of the Netherlands, because the fugitive Jos L., alias Bolle Jos, has found shelter in the African country. He is said to have close ties there with people in high positions, including the president. Hundred years in prison L. is called the most wanted criminal of the Low Countries. In the Netherlands he has been sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted assassination, in Belgium he has received more than a hundred years in prison in various cases combined. "I am very happy with this step," Van Weel says in the Telegraaf . "It is bitter that EU money goes to a country that does not want to cooperate with the extradition of someone like Bolle Jos." The Dutch minister hopes that this will be seen as a firm statement, that not only the Netherlands but the entire European Union disapproves of Sierra Leone's unwillingness. Tightening sanctions Within the EU, possibilities are being examined to further tighten the sanctions policy for criminals staying outside Europe, for example by imposing an entry ban or freezing financial assets. Van Weel is now in Luxembourg for a meeting of European justice ministers, where this will also be discussed. The European Parliament recently adopted a resolution stating that "persons convicted of serious drug trafficking offences must not escape prosecution." The Dutch drug baron Jos L. is mentioned by name in it.

title: Cabinet is prepared to spare smaller savers and investors after all
lead: The minority cabinet is prepared to amend the plans for the wealth tax in such a way that smaller savers and investors are spared. That is what <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> said on the second day of the Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen. He did warn that it is "enormously complicated" to find an alternative that yields just as much. To free up money for the introduction of a profit tax on investments in box 3, the cabinet proposed making small investors and savers pay tax earlier and more from 2028. The exemption would go down, so that people would already be taxed if they earn more than a thousand euros per year in returns on their savings or investments. That plan was received very poorly by both the left-wing and right-wing opposition, as became clear yesterday. With that, the cabinet could not count on a majority for the budget. The parliamentary groups of the coalition parties also indicated they were not happy with it. Not many knobs to turn Minister Heinen said today that he chose that threshold because a couple with savings of up to about 100,000 euros is then exempt. But he also acknowledged today that the lower limit may not have been chosen so well after all. Many people who currently pay no tax on their savings will suddenly have to do so. He underestimated that. "We are prepared to consider a different threshold," he said. It does mean that money must be found elsewhere in the tax sphere, and according to Heinen that is difficult. "We do not have very many knobs to turn. And every choice you make is enormously complicated. It takes a lot of calculation work." Temporary tax increase In <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> there is also much concern about a temporary tax increase on wealth for next year. The exemption would then be lowered from just under 60,000 euros to about 31,000 euros. The percentage of tax that people pay would also go up. The minister will look into that too and wants to consult with the Tweede Kamer about a different lower limit from 2028. In two weeks, when the Belastingplan is discussed in the Kamer, there must be clarity. 'Polder must deliver' The debate also covered scrapping the cuts to social security. Heinen said that he expects that if a social agreement is reached between employers and trade unions, it will yield more money than the cabinet had initially budgeted with the cut. According to him, the social partners have said they can fulfil that promise. The consequence of a social agreement should be that less money is spent on benefits such as the WW and the WIA. But if an agreement in the 'polder' is not reached, or the reforms yield too little, then the money must be found by cutting the expenditures of the ministries. On Tuesday it became clear that in that case the Ministry of Education would be hit hardest: in the extreme case, 1.2 billion euros must be saved there. Education Minister Letschert said yesterday that there is no coalition agreement to cut education. Heinen stated today in the debate that the saving is "technically booked", but that it will never take place if the social partners fulfil their promise. "Then it is a non-discussion," said Heinen.

title: Minister Van Weel: Sierra Leone can resolve Bolle Jos conflict within 24 hours
lead: Sierra Leone can solve its problem with the European Commission immediately by extraditing drug criminal Bolle Jos to the Netherlands. That is what Minister Van Weel of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> says from Luxembourg. This morning it became known that the European Commission has stopped budget support for <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of the African country. The country would still receive 18 million this year for, for example, food programmes, education and infrastructure. Van Weel is in Luxembourg for a meeting of European justice ministers. They will discuss, among other things, tightening sanctions against fugitive criminals staying outside Europe. The Dutch minister is pleased that the money tap to Sierra Leone has now been turned off. "It is a very clear signal from the European Commission that Sierra Leone must stop offering shelter to this criminal." 'Building pressure' When asked whether the measure is not too crude, he points to the government of the impoverished country. It is protecting a criminal "who destroys an enormous amount, also for the population of Sierra Leone," he says. "They can solve this within 24 hours by picking up this man and extraditing him." If this punitive measure does not help, "we will continue building the pressure through other routes," says Van Weel. "It is of the utmost importance to us to get this criminal to the Netherlands." Bolle Jos L. is called the most wanted criminal of the Low Countries. In the Netherlands he has been sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted assassination, in Belgium he has received more than a hundred years in prison across various cases combined.

title: Cabinet to meet again with unions and employers on Wednesday after months of postponement
lead: Next Wednesday, the trade unions and employers will sit down with the cabinet for the first time in months to talk about the future of social security. The cabinet has invited six organisations, VNO-NCW, MKB NL, LTO, FNV, CNV and VCP, to come to the Catshuis on Wednesday. On behalf of the cabinet, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and the three most involved ministers Vijlbrief (Social Affairs), Aartsen (Work and Participation) and Herbert (<entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-ez">Economische Zaken</entity>) will attend. The unions FNV and CNV will come to The Hague, the organisations say. This makes it likely that the other organisations will also accept the invitation. Since the end of May, the unions have no longer been talking with the cabinet about the retrenchment of social security, the schemes that exist to help Dutch people who cannot work or are retired. In May there was a Catshuis consultation about this, but opinions turned out to diverge so widely that it remained at one conversation. Talks would only resume, the unions made clear time and again, if the Jetten cabinet scrapped the planned cuts. The unions also announced actions. Retrenchments The Jetten cabinet initially wanted to cut some 6 billion euros by raising the AOW age more quickly, and retrenchments in WW and WIA (disabled) schemes. The cabinet already withdrew the AOW plan earlier, but the unions - supported by the largest opposition party Pro - continued to insist on their demand that all cuts in social security had to be reversed. The cabinet has now done this at the start of this week, and now the talks with the 'polder' are being restarted. Long-term The unions recognise, just like the employers and the cabinet, that the problems must be solved, especially with the WIA, the Wet, Werk en Inkomen naar Arbeidsvermogen. Around 60,000 people flow into the WIA each year, often young people and women with psychological problems. There is a large shortage of insurance physicians and the waiting lists are long. "We must not wait until people drop out long-term, but prevent that," the unions FNV, CNV and VCP wrote in a joint press release at the start of this week.

title: Van Weel sticks to his position: halting support to Sierra Leone linked to Bolle Jos
lead: <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> says there is no tension between him and the European Commission about halting support to Sierra Leone. He maintains that it is a means of pressure, which must lead to the extradition of drug criminal Jos L. Yesterday Van Weel announced that European support has been ended because of Sierra Leone's unwillingness to extradite L. Those statements caused irritation behind the scenes at the European Commission. The halting of the payments would be a purely technical matter and not a sanction to bring <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of Sierra Leone to its knees. But Van Weel sticks to his story. "I am glad that the European Commission has found a legal way to do this and I think it helps in building the pressure on Sierra Leone," he said this morning in the run-up to <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. The minister repeated that he is "on a mission" to get Jos L., alias Bolle Jos, extradited. He says he shuns no means and "also wants to enter into the confrontation with Sierra Leone, if I think it is in the interest of this dossier". Diplomacy That there is irritation about this within the European Commission is not known to him. "I do not know the sources behind the scenes." He has only spoken with European Commissioner Brunner, who is responsible for tackling organised crime. And "there really was no tension there, we have a good relationship." According to Van Weel, Brunner did indeed make a link with Bolle Jos at a press conference yesterday, albeit in a less explicit way. In a subordinate clause the European Commissioner said: "We need the cooperation of Sierra Leone. That is what it is about." That the European Commission outwardly cites a technical reason to pause the development aid has to do with diplomacy, among other things, he thinks. But Van Weel himself opts for a "direct confrontation" with the country that protects the fugitive criminal. "I chose that because I see that, besides diplomacy, we must build up the pressure in another way." Sierra Leone would still receive 18 million euros in budget support from Brussels this year. That was suspended with immediate effect yesterday. As far as the Netherlands is concerned, the payment of 22.5 million for next year will also not go ahead, if Bolle Jos has still not been extradited by then.

title: Excise duty on vapes in over two years
lead: Vapes (e-cigarettes) and refills will become euros more expensive as of 1 January 2029 because the government will levy more tax on these products. Users already pay 21 percent VAT. In over two years, excise duty will be added on top of that. "It is shocking how many young people are now on the vapes," says <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. "If consumers see that it becomes considerably more expensive, they will think twice before spending their money on unhealthy junk." Flavour ban The rules for vapes are now virtually the same as for ordinary cigarettes and tobacco smoking products. Since 1 January 2024, there has been an official ban on flavoured vapes. The flavour tobacco is still permitted. Where smoking bans apply, that also applies to vapes. Points of sale of e-cigarettes must register just like tobacco shops. The expectation is that as of 1 July 2027 or as of 1 January 2028, the sale of vapes will only be allowed in specialty shops. Eerenberg: "It cannot be explained that only ordinary cigarettes are extra taxed to ensure that people do not smoke. It should make no difference whether you do one or the other." The vape excise duties still have to be calculated but will be comparable to those on tobacco products. Harmful Vapes, like tobacco products, are harmful to health. In a vape, liquid with or without nicotine is heated so that vapour is created. No combustion of tobacco takes place, so no tar or carbon monoxide is released. However, users do ingest chemical substances. If excise duties on vapes are introduced at European level earlier than on 1 January 2029, then <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will withdraw this proposal again.

title: Podcast De Dag: David van Weel's hunt for Bolle Jos
lead: Sierra Leone will receive millions less from Europe this year. Justice Minister Van Weel said yesterday that this was decided because the country does not want to extradite Bolle Jos to the Netherlands. From Brussels, a different reason was heard shortly afterwards, of a technical nature. This morning Van Weel says that both are correct and that Europe stands behind him in his hunt for Bolle Jos. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. What is Minister Van Weel trying to do to catch the drug criminal? Political reporter Jorn Jonker sees a determined minister who, despite personal consequences, tries everything in his hunt for Bolle Jos. But are all those steps also useful? Sierra Leone expert at Clingendael Institute Kars de Bruijne sees cracks emerging in the drug criminal's empire. But extradition is, after all those steps, anything but closer. Respond? Mail to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial staff: Marco Geijtenbeek & Max Smedes

title: Podcast De Stemming: Hyperfocus, financial charlatans and the Tweelcos
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> spoke last weekend and on Monday with various opposition parties about support for the budget. And that suddenly produced a breakthrough after <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> had scrapped the cuts in social security. But where you remove a cut in one budget, as a rule one is added in another. And that in turn led to confusion and unrest in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. Podcast De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister . There you will also find all previous episodes . Just like at all other well-known podcast channels . About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings ( EenVandaag , AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) review the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Do you want to respond? Then email destemming@nos.nl.

title: Jetten on box 3 uncertainty: 'I understand if people can no longer keep up'
lead: "I can imagine that people can no longer keep up with it", admits <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> about the uncertainty that has arisen around box 3. For a moment, hundreds of thousands of smaller investors and savers thought that they too would have to pay tax on their assets. But after a day and a half that plan was already off the table . The coalition had by then already taken days to reach internal agreement on a new plan for box 3. That was finished at the last minute, on the evening before the Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen. The next day it turned out that not only the opposition was critical, but it also became clear that coalition parties had little appetite for taxing smaller savers and investors. And so <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) could do nothing else a day and a half later than admit that he had not thought through the funding properly. "A minority cabinet is tough", sighed the VVD minister on his way into <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. 'Fear of a left-wing agenda' VVD deputy prime minister Yesilgöz also found it "not a nice week", because of the "noise, commotion and perception" around the Belastingplan. According to her, that has caused "fear of a left-wing agenda" among the VVD base. As far as she is concerned, the emphasis should mainly be on what the right did secure, such as the lower excise duty on petrol, the lower tax in box 2 and the lower aviation tax. That there is now any majority at all for an accelerated capital gains tax in box 3 is also seen by the VVD as a major victory. "If you explain it factually, people understand very well what we are doing. The mega problem around box 3 is now being solved in 2028", Yesilgöz said at the ministerraad. "Until two months ago no one thought that was possible." Still, there are quite a few hurdles to clear. Accelerating the introduction of the capital gains tax is estimated to cost 15 billion euros. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> must now come up with a new plan for the funding within a few weeks, in order to still achieve introduction in 2028. One of the options mentioned is to abolish a construction around the inheritance tax, the gift on paper. That option too is sensitive for the VVD and other parties on the right. What is the solution that has now been proposed for box 3? You can read that in this article: The coalition still hopes to find "broad support" for the Belastingplan, in which it is agreed how the government will collect tax in the coming years. It is still unclear how. Both Pro and JA21, parties that are needed for a majority, want to give support only if income tax goes down. The negotiations are made extra complicated because some parties want to agree to the Belastingplan only if the cabinet meets other conditions. For example, BBB wants the nitrogen plans to be adjusted and SGP wants abortions to be reduced. Steam and boiling water The cabinet now has a few more weeks to find a majority, because on 12 November <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> votes on the Belastingplan. In the meantime, the legislative amendment for box 3 must also be rushed through the Eerste and Tweede Kamer. "If the discussion is mainly about the funding of the proposal, that can always be resolved", Jetten remains optimistic. A boost for the cabinet is in any case that the trade unions will be back at the table next Wednesday . Then the discussion begins about reforms in the WW and the WIA, which according to the cabinet must ultimately also yield savings.

title: VVD leader Yesilgöz very rosy about the atmosphere within the party: yet members cancelling
lead: VVD leader Yesilgöz presented her supporters' reaction to the adjusted cabinet plans in a very rosy way. She reported that new VVD members had joined, but that is not the whole story, as appears from inquiries into the number of VVD members cancelling this week. At the start of <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity> Yesilgöz was asked by journalists this morning whether it had been a tough week for her party. The VVD leader began by listing that much also went well for her supporters. For instance, many people are happy that a solution has been found for box 3, the wealth tax, said Yesilgöz. And, she reported: "We also have dozens of new members". The VVD party office has kept track of what happened to the membership number since the adjusted cabinet plans were presented on Tuesday evening. From that moment until Thursday, according to the party, 78 cancellations had actually come in. In those few days there were also 21 new registrations. A spokesperson for the party office says that what Yesilgöz stated is therefore not incorrect. 'Explode' Within the VVD, dissatisfaction can be noted about the cabinet plans adjusted this week. Members whom NOS spoke to talk about app groups that seem to "explode". Especially because <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> initially wanted more savers and investors to pay tax in box 3. It also does not go down well that, for example, landlords and people with a second home will have to pay more. There are also groups of members who think that the cuts in social security were abandoned too easily. They believe that reforms are still needed on that subject. Some also have the feeling that a bow has been made toward opposition party Pro, while during the campaign it was promised that the VVD would not go in that direction. Fred Teeven, former officeholder for the party, said this week on Nieuws van de Dag: "I see many people taking leave of the VVD. If they want to retain any representation in the Provincial Council, they had better watch out". Nuance According to a spokesperson for Yesilgöz, the party leader is not at all running away from the fact that there are also cancellations. The politician would only have wanted to nuance the image that is being sketched these days - that the whole world is negative about the VVD - by saying that new members have also joined. VVD <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> of Infrastructure said this morning that it was a "turbulent week" for his party. He emphasized that much unrest among his supporters subsides when it is explained what has been secured for the VVD in the adjusted cabinet plans. According to Karremans, the VVD suffers from the image that the party is so positive about scrapping the cuts in social security. Right-wing people then get the idea that the package will turn out badly for them if Pro is so positive, reasons the VVD member. While according to him much has indeed been agreed for the VVD supporters, such as a rapid conversion to a capital gains tax. "That is somewhat snowed under, under the smile of Jesse Klaver. But if you look under the hood, I think there is a solid package."

title: State Secretary for ban on unstunned slaughter: 'Remove the taboo'
lead: <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> of Agriculture believes that, as in Belgium, a ban should be introduced on the unstunned slaughter of animals. He uses World Animal Day to make clear that unstunned slaughter does not belong in the Netherlands because of animal welfare, he said this morning on the television programme WNL op Zondag . In an interview with RTL Nieuws that was published this morning, Erkens had already said that he "personally" believes that unstunned ritual slaughter fits poorly within the cabinet's policy to improve animal welfare in the Netherlands. The discussion about unstunned slaughter has been going on for almost fifteen years and has become topical again because the Partij voor de Dieren is submitting a bill again this month to ensure that animals are no longer slaughtered before they are stunned. Razor-sharp According to certain Islamic and Jewish religious prescriptions, animals must be slaughtered without stunning. In the Netherlands, this now happens according to all kinds of rules to limit animal suffering. In a slaughterhouse, an animal receives a cut in the neck with a razor-sharp knife from a certified so-called 'voorsnijder'. If the animal has not died within forty seconds, it must still be stunned. State Secretary Erkens considers that a long period for an animal. "That is forty seconds of animal suffering," he said on WNL op Zondag . He believes that the taboo on the subject must be removed. Complex He himself will not make a law to put an end to unstunned slaughter in the Netherlands and mainly makes clear that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is positive about the Partij voor de Dieren's bill. "It is a complex subject that touches on freedom of religion." He emphasises that a law must be introduced that is legally sustainable. The Partij voor de Dieren already came up with an initiative bill in 2011 for a ban on ritual slaughter. In <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> the law failed, a majority of senators believed that it was in conflict with freedom of religion. The Partij voor de Dieren then continued with drafting an amended law, which was also positively received by the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>. Impact MP Ouwehand, drafter of this law, emphasises that not only religious slaughter was looked at, but also regular slaughter. "It is important to conduct the debate carefully, because this has an impact on the Jewish and Islamic faith communities." She is pleased that State Secretary Erkens now clearly acknowledges that animal welfare is important in Dutch society. On WNL op Zondag , Erkens emphasised that ritual slaughter does not have to come to an end, as long as the animal is stunned. He says that half of the ritual slaughters in the Netherlands already happen in this way. An animal is then temporarily stunned. That is acceptable to some religious groups, because the animal is then not dead.

title: Cabinet tightens advice on screen use, phones in the safe all school day
lead: The cabinet wants primary schools and secondary schools to ban the use of mobile phones throughout the entire school from 1 January 2027. Pupils will then also no longer be allowed to use their phones during breaks, in the canteen or in the schoolyard. Currently, at many schools pupils are only not allowed to take their phone into the classroom. This is one of the proposals from the so-called 'Strategy letter online children's rights', in which, under the leadership of <entity id="person:willemijn-aerdts">staatssecretaris Aerdts</entity> (Digital Economy), various ministries have listed new and existing rules to better protect children online. The cabinet does not have authority over pupils' phone use at Dutch schools, but can issue an urgent advice. That also happened in 2024, when the Ministry of Education made national agreements with primary schools on restricting mobile phones during lessons.
