The cabinet wants the tightened advice to take effect on 1 January 2027 in secondary schools and in primary education. Scrolling The cabinet, like many parents and other institutions, is concerned about the increasing online use of Dutch children and young people. At school children are distracted and can concentrate less well. For parents at home, for example, it proves difficult to curb their children's hours-long scrolling. Due to addictive algorithms and auto-playing videos, it proves very difficult to put the phone down, and daily screen times of around 5 to 6 hours are not unusual. Experts have long warned about the negative consequences of excessive screen use, such as sleep problems, nearsightedness and depression. Furthermore, it is unclear what young people are exactly viewing and there is poor oversight of cyberbullying or other unsavoury matters. Unwanted contact Several ministries have long been committed with various plans to offer young people sufficient protection against everything there is to view online. Today staatssecretaris Aerdts presents a strategy for a "safe and healthy online world for children", with around forty regulations, of which according to her fifteen are new. "Online, on social media or in video games, children quickly slip out of sight and run unacceptable risks", the staatssecretaris said. "Think of addictive algorithms, harmful images and unwanted contact." A number of measures from the Strategy letter have been in the works for longer, because they are a matter of the long haul. The European Commission recently made a proposal for an age limit on social media. The European Commission is thinking of 13 years, the Dutch cabinet of 15 years. Other proposals include, for example, banning addictive techniques such as algorithms in the design of digital services at European level. Work must also be done on a reliable system of age verification, in which the privacy of young people is well protected. Child labour The cabinet is also working on stricter rules for buy now, pay later services, such as the deferred payment service Klarna. The cabinet will also continue working out tightened rules for vlog families and kidfluencers. Online content of children under 15 years will be regarded as child labour and can be fined as such. The cabinet is also having research done into Netflix, YouTube, Roblox, Fortnite, ChatGPT, Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok to "gain better insight into how digital services influence the experience, development and choices of children who use digital services". The most concrete measure, banning mobile phones in and around schools, must according to the cabinet therefore take effect in three months. <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> of Education will now make agreements about this with the education sector.

title: Introducing capital gains tax in 2028 becomes a race against the clock
lead: <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> promised <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> last week to do everything in his power to introduce the new capital gains tax as early as 2028. It will be a race against the clock, with those involved wondering whether it will all succeed. On Friday, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> sent the legislative amendment that must make the new system possible to the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> for advice. Many MPs wondered whether that advice would be in time for the next parliamentary debate on this, on 12 October. Heinen was optimistic on Thursday: "Wij vragen een maximale stretch van iedereen, maar dan is 2028 haalbaar." Although he also acknowledged the risk that it becomes 2029. A rapid introduction of the new wealth tax is politically important for Heinen. It was an important commitment to right-wing opposition parties such as JA21 and the SGP. The Raad van State says on request that it will certainly not meet the deadline of 12 October. "We hebben nog maar zeven dagen, onmogelijk", a spokesperson states. The advice will come at the earliest on 19 October, and possibly only on the 26th. That makes it even tighter for the Kamer to deal with the law in time. Fraud lurking The banks say on request that they have too little time to adjust their IT systems. As a result, it will not be possible to have their customers' data pre-filled when they file their tax returns in 2028. The banks had already warned about this, but <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of Financiën suggested last week that there would be a solution for this. According to him, many banks have recently spoken out in favour of the new capital gains tax. "Ik vind dus dat we ook iets mogen vragen als: nu moet u ook uw cliënten helpen om dat mogelijk te maken." The Nederlandse Vereniging van Banken does not recognise that. "Wij hebben nooit een voorkeur uitgesproken voor belasting op vermogenswinst of vermogensaanwas." There will soon be a meeting with the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> to see what is possible as long as the pre-filled returns are not there, a spokesperson says. If the banks and asset managers cannot supply the data, the Belastingdienst cannot check whether citizens have filled in the return correctly. And then fraud is lurking. For people who fill in their return in good faith, it is questionable whether they can find the information themselves. Not all banks can provide the data directly to their customers. It makes filling in the return more complicated in any case. Officials of Financiën already warned about this in an advice : "Dit doet een extra beroep op het 'doenvermogen' van burgers." Even if the above problems are solved, it will be quite a feat for the Belastingdienst to implement the system change by 2028. The service is namely also busy with adjustments to the computer systems, because from 2030 there will be a mandatory disability insurance for self-employed people. If both adjustments have to be carried out at the same time, the introduction of that insurance will probably be delayed by a year, officials warned. Last week the kabinet made a new proposal for an accelerated transition to a capital gains tax, as a replacement for the current wealth accumulation tax. The VVD was under great pressure from its supporters, because investors object to paying tax on 'paper profit', in other words, tax on shares that have not yet been sold and have only increased in value on paper. Paying upon sale But if citizens only start paying when the shares have been sold, billions of euros less tax will come in temporarily. The kabinet wanted to fill that gap by also making smaller savers and investors pay capital gains tax, but there turned out to be no majority for that in the Tweede Kamer. In the proposal that has been sent to the Raad van State, remarkably enough, that cover rejected by the Kamer is still included. Meanwhile, the kabinet is looking for alternatives, in consultation with opposition parties. That means that new adjustments to box 3 are still coming, also for next year. If it does not succeed in getting the legislation through the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> this year, the current system will remain in force for at least another year. Every year of delay costs the treasury 3.5 billion euros in lost revenue. Eerste Kamer Tonight Heinen and Eerenberg will give text and explanation in the Eerste Kamer. The senators have postponed votes on the plans with box 3 time and again, at the request of the kabinet. And now there is haste. Senator Crone of Pro is indignant about that state of affairs: "Dit gaat om een grote stelselwijziging. Die moeten we zorgvuldig behandelen, met onder meer het horen van deskundigen." His colleague Griffioen of governing party D66 urges the kabinet to use the short time that remains well: "Het kabinet is aan zet om dit goed te regelen, treuzel niet en kom met goede voorstellen."

title: Cabinet wants to link public transport and other transport in the region
lead: Het kabinet wil de verschraling van het openbaar vervoer in de regio tegengaan door het ov en andere soorten vervoer, zoals het leerlingenvervoer, aan elkaar te koppelen. Ook moeten er proeven komen met zelfrijdende bussen. <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> van <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> schrijft in twee brieven aan <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> dat zij zich grote zorgen maakt over de bereikbaarheid in de regio. Ze wil er "met de beschikbare middelen" naar kijken dat bijvoorbeeld ook ziekenhuizen en culturele instellingen beter bereikbaar worden. Ze wijst erop dat er naast het reguliere ov al allerlei alternatieven zijn, zoals regiotaxi's, belbusjes, buurtbussen en deelauto's. Die werken echter veelal nog langs elkaar heen. Zo zie je busjes achter elkaar naar dezelfde plek rijden, de ene keer voor leerlingen- en de andere keer voor WMO-vervoer voor mensen die niet zelfstandig met het ov kunnen reizen. Wat haar betreft kan er veel efficiënter worden samengewerkt. 'Fijnmazig netwerk' Bertram ziet een "fijnmazig netwerk van publiek vervoer" voor zich, waarin een belangrijke rol is weggelegd voor een mobiliteitscentrale waar alle aanvragen binnenkomen en "kenmerken van alle reizigers" bekend zijn, zodat "de beschikbare voertuigen" optimaal ingezet kunnen worden. Verder wil de staatssecretaris drie proeven gaan doen met zelfrijdende bussen. Er rijdt sinds vorig jaar al zo'n bus in Rotterdam, die mensen van een metrostation naar het vliegveld vervoert. De staatssecretaris vreest een neerwaartse spiraal als het gaat om bereikbaarheid buiten steden. Minder ouderen kunnen in drie kwartier bij een ziekenhuis komen, merkt ze. Het ANP meldde deze week dat 1100 bushaltes zijn verdwenen in de afgelopen zes jaar, vooral in Drenthe en Groningen. Haperen "Het huidige systeem begint te haperen", concludeert Bertram. Vervoerders kampen met tekorten aan chauffeurs, terwijl bussen buiten de spits juist vaak leeg rondrijden. Op Prinsjesdag kondigde het kabinet aan jaarlijks een bedrag van 300 miljoen euro uit te trekken om regionale bereikbaarheid te verbeteren. Later deze maand maakt de bewindsvrouw bekend hoe zij dit geld gaat inzetten.

title: Italian dogs must deter wolves on heathland in Ermelo
lead: Sheep on the Ermelosche Heide have had bodyguards in the form of two Italian dogs since this summer. The white mountain dogs must protect the flock against wolves. "Through their presence, the wolf must think: not today, then," shepherd Marion Derks tells Omroep Gelderland. The Schapedrift Ermelo foundation had already placed the flock behind wolf-resistant fences with electric wire. "But when we went out, our animals were not protected." The foundation therefore decided to bring two dogs from Italy to Ermelo to protect the flock at all times. "We had increasing threat from the wolf. And a few were also walking around here that were interested in the sheep," says Derks. Barking The breed, called the Maremma and Abruzzo Shepherd Dog, has been used for centuries to protect livestock. "As soon as they see danger, you see their posture change and they go into protection mode. Then they make themselves bigger and more robust and start barking." It is not intended that the wolf and the dogs engage in a fight. "But through their presence, the wolf must not come near the sheep. The wolf takes an easy prey and if he thinks it is becoming too difficult, he will look for something else." According to the foundation, the new four-legged friends are not dangerous to walkers. "We deliberately chose this breed, because they are not as fierce as other dogs. We of course deal with a lot of tourism and this breed is relatively calm," Derks explains. Closed off to other dogs However, the dogs can react fiercely if an animal or person approaches the sheep at high speed. "So get off if you are on a bicycle and do not pass the flock at full gallop with your horse," warns the shepherd. The dogs live with the sheep day and night. Since the arrival of the two mountain dogs, parts of the heathland have been prohibited for other dogs. "That way the Abruzzo Maremmas can get used to the routine we have. If we encounter many dogs, that hinders the development." The dog ban has been in effect since 15 August and is expected to last six months in total.

title: Separatists in Quebec win elections, blow for Prime Minister Carney
lead: In the Canadian province of Quebec, the separatist Parti Quebecois (PQ) narrowly won the local elections. The victory of PQ, which wants to make Quebec independent from Canada, is a setback for Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. His national government is coming under pressure. Canada has been embroiled in a trade conflict with the United States since this summer. According to the Canadian prime minister, it is therefore important to act jointly with all provinces against US President Trump. The separatists of PQ, under the leadership of Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, are not eager for that unity. Plamondon actually wants to confront the prime minister. As soon as Trump has left the White House, he wants to hold a referendum on an independent Quebec. "A referendum is a chance to decide about ourselves," says PQ leader Plamondon. "One day we will achieve our national goal." Referendum uncertain Yet it is not certain whether that will succeed. A referendum requires a majority, but PQ won 59 of the 127 parliamentary seats; that is 5 too few for a majority. The separatists must therefore find support from other parties. "The residents of Quebec elected us with the task of working with other parties. And I have heard that message," says Plamondon. Earlier attempts by PQ for a referendum failed in 1980 and 1995. Even if a popular vote comes, it is anything but certain that Quebec will become independent. Recent polls show that support for an independent Quebec, at 30 percent, is at one of its lowest levels ever. According to political scientist Daniel Béland, the fact that PQ nevertheless wins now is mainly due to the unpopularity of the incumbent power, the Coalition Avenir Quebec (CAQ). "These elections were not about independence, but about getting rid of the CAQ," he tells news agency AP. Voters dissatisfied According to analysts, the election result in Quebec makes dissatisfaction with the government visible. The CAQ party has been in power in the province since 2018. In these elections, the party lost all 79 seats. Party leader Christine Fréchette speaks of a "difficult result". Next month, residents of the energy-rich province of Alberta can make their voices heard about the independence of their province. A non-binding referendum on this is being organized there on 19 October. Congratulations Carney Prime Minister Carney has congratulated PQ party leader Plamondon and says he wants to work with the separatists. "A stronger Quebec contributes to a stronger Canada," says Carney. The prime minister spoke, among other things, about cooperation to help businesses and workers affected by American import tariffs. Political scientist Béland is less optimistic than the prime minister. "That a pro-independence party wins in Quebec, less than two weeks before an independence referendum comes in Alberta, radiates problems with our unity toward the Trump administration." The predominantly French-speaking province of Quebec has more than nine million inhabitants. Canada has a total of more than 41 million inhabitants.

title: American evangelist Jim Bakker died, known for TV and scandals
lead: The American TV evangelist Jim Bakker has died at the age of 86. He became known in the 70s and 80s, when he presented the program The PTL-Club, an abbreviation for Praise The Lord . Later he became embroiled in controversy because of bribing churchgoers and false medical claims. His wife, Lori Bakker, announced the death via Facebook. "With a broken heart I share that my beloved husband, Jim Bakker, has gone to the Lord tonight," she writes. What the TV preacher died of has not been made known. Bakker gained fame with his ex-wife, Tammy Faye, who died in 2007. They met at North Central Bible College in Minneapolis and married in 1961. The couple did puppet theater together in a church, after which they were asked to perform it on TV. The Bakkers then presented the Christian program The 700 Club between 1966 and 1973. Later they started a television channel of their own: The Inspiration Network. Here they started the Christian talk show The PTL-Club . At its peak, the program brought in more than 128 million dollars per year and was broadcast via 1300 cable networks with 12 million subscribers. Fraud and conspiracy Behind the scenes, cracks slowly appeared in the story of the happy couple who presented the show together. Bakker resigned in 1987 after his affair with secretary Jessica Hahn came to light. To keep quiet about this, he paid her a one-time 115,000 dollars, followed by monthly payments. A year later, Bakker was charged with fraud and conspiracy to defraud churchgoers of 158 million dollars. In 1989 he was found guilty by a jury. He was given a prison sentence of 45 years. While he was in prison, Tammy Faye Bakker divorced him. Their life story was made into the film The Eyes of Tammy Faye with Jessica Chastain and Andrew Garfield. In 1992 his prison sentence was reduced to eight years. Two years later Bakker was released on parole, after serving almost five years of his sentence. Married again After his release, in the 90s he met Lori Graham at the Dream Center in Los Angeles, an organization that focuses on disadvantaged young people. They married that same year. Bakker slowly returned to the stage. From 2003 he presented the program The Jim Bakker Show with his new wife. But again he became embroiled in controversy. In 2020 he praised silver supplements as a medicine for corona. The attorney general of New York ordered the TV evangelist to stop making false medical claims. Several TV channels removed Bakker's program from their channel. Later Bakker reached a settlement in the case. He was no longer allowed to claim that silver solution helped against a disease or condition. People who had previously bought this received compensation.

title: Former head of German intelligence arrested for espionage
lead: The former head of the German intelligence service BND August Hanning has been detained. According to German media, Hanning is suspected among other things of espionage, high treason and making state secrets public. The German Public Prosecution Service has confirmed his arrest. Hanning headed the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND) from 1998 to 2005. Among other things, he is said to have bought secret information from a BND employee until 2022. He is said to have used this information to draw up a security analysis for a foreign intelligence service. Which country is not known, but according to German media it would not be Russia. In addition, he is said to have shared internal information with a foreign agent. House search The 80-year-old Hanning was arrested at his home this morning. The former employee, who held a high position at the service, has also been arrested. The man was previously an important right-hand man of Hanning and worked for the BND until the spring. The authorities got on the trail of the case after they had conducted a house search at Hanning's home in September last year because of a kidnapping case. In the investigation into that, a tip came in that information may have been leaked from the BND. Hanning may also be involved in the kidnapping itself, although he has always denied this. During the house search, agents discovered highly sensitive information originating from the BND. The secret documents came from the recent past and so Hanning should never have possessed them. According to sources, Hanning is said to have received around 2000 documents and they would include reports about the Iranian nuclear programme and the Russian army. Key positions During his career, Hanning held key positions at the German security services for years. After his period at the BND, as State Secretary of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> he was among other things responsible for security, after which he went into business. In recent years, Hanning worked among other things as a consultant in the security and business world. He did so in places all over the world. German media report that he has good connections with Russia and China and the government bodies there.

title: Measles outbreak in New York and Pennsylvania largest since the 1990s
lead: Measles is spreading rapidly in the American states of New York and Pennsylvania. In New York a state of emergency has even been declared, after more than a hundred people were infected this week. Due to the state of emergency, aid workers can intervene more quickly and, for example, may test and distribute vaccines more quickly. In Pennsylvania, the number of registered measles cases this year has passed the threshold of a thousand. This makes it one of the largest outbreaks since the early 1990s. Nearly two hundred patients have been admitted to hospital and five people have died. Health experts link such outbreaks to the declining vaccination rate in the US. In other states too, such as Texas, Utah and South Carolina, large outbreaks have been reported since the beginning of last year. What is measles? Measles is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by a virus. A measles infection usually runs a mild course, but serious complications can occur and the patient can die from it. Figures from the WHO show that in 2024 approximately 95,000 people worldwide died of measles, particularly children under the age of 5. You can recognise measles by a sudden high fever, red eyes, coughing, a cold and red spots on the skin that often feel rough. In the Netherlands, more than five hundred people contracted measles last year, especially children at primary schools where few pupils were vaccinated. In the Netherlands there is a jab against measles, which is the MMR vaccine. Besides Pennsylvania and New York, Ohio is also dealing with a serious measles outbreak: more than 200 infections have already been confirmed there this year. As in Pennsylvania, some of the hardest-hit areas in Ohio are home to strictly Christian Amish communities, where the vaccination rate is generally lower. According to the American health institute CDC, the US is experiencing the worst measles outbreak nationwide since 1991, with a total of now nearly 4000 cases. About twenty percent of these are children under the age of five. In the past two years, eight people have died from complications related to measles. That is more deaths than in the thirty years before that combined. Deaths In February 2025, Robert F. Kennedy jr. was appointed Minister of Health in the <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>-Trump. For years he was one of the loudest vaccine critics in the US. For example, shortly after taking office he dismissed all the experts of the advisory committee for vaccines and partly replaced them with vaccine sceptics. After several deaths from measles, he somewhat softened his positions on the disease. For example, he declared that the MMR vaccine is the most effective way to prevent the spread of the disease. But in the meantime the consequences of his criticism are already becoming apparent. The vaccination rate is now already below the 95 percent needed to curb the spread of measles. As a result, the infection figures are rising rapidly in several states. In November, international health officials will meet to determine whether the US and Mexico have lost their status as a measles-free country. A country must have no cases of the disease for twelve months to be declared measles-free. Disinformation about vaccines and problems with access to healthcare also lead to some parents not vaccinating themselves or their children. Salmonella Besides measles outbreaks, the US is also struggling with a number of foodborne diseases. For example, this year nearly 13,000 Americans got diarrhoea and other stomach and abdominal complaints from eating lettuce contaminated with the intestinal parasite. The American food and drug authority FDA has now traced the contamination to a Mexican farm. American media write that food products in the US are increasingly being recalled because of contamination with bacteria, viruses or parasites. This concerns among other things eggs, chicken or meat. According to various media, this development is caused by budget cuts and the departure of staff at the FDA and the American Department of Agriculture, which puts food inspections under pressure. The American health service CDC is currently investigating 33 outbreaks of food-related diseases, including salmonella, E. coli and listeria.

title: Drone attack on ships off Bulgarian coast, prime minister holds emergency meeting
lead: Off the coast of Bulgaria in the Black Sea, a ship sank after a drone attack. On another ship fire broke out, Bulgarian president Iotova confirms in a statement. According to prime minister Radev, the crew of the sunken ship is missing. It is not clear how many people it concerns. A search has been started for them. Eighteen crew members were rescued from the burning ship. Some have been taken to the hospital in Varna, on the east coast of Bulgaria. Local media write that one of them has severe burns, another would be injured in the head. A number of others have minor injuries. Cargo ships According to media sources, it concerns cargo ships. The sunken ship, named Alfa Watan, sailed under the flag of Togo. It is not known what cargo the ship was carrying. The ship where fire broke out, named Able, sailed under the flag of Palau. Of that ship it is known that it was carrying grain. The attack took place around 03:00 local time some 112 kilometres from the coast, still in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. That country is a member of NATO. After the incident, both ships sent out distress signals. Bulgarian prime minister Radev held an emergency meeting with involved ministries and security services. It is not yet clear whether it concerns an attack with drones in the air, sea drones or both. Reference to war Russia and Ukraine Who is behind the drone attack is not yet clear. However, the Bulgarian prime minister referred in a statement on television to the Russian war in Ukraine. News agency Reuters writes based on a source in the field of maritime security that initial analyses of the attack indicate that it was probably a Russian attack. "If this war is not ended in time, the risk of a global conflict grows," said prime minister Radev. "We see that the war is escalating: all rules of international law are being violated and civilian ships are attacked at sea. This is completely unacceptable." Russia has not yet responded to the event. Fire on Turkish ship The attack follows shortly after a fire on a ship in the Black Sea yesterday, outside Romania's territorial waters. Two people died, eleven crew members could be rescued. The Romanian ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> says it is not yet known what the cause of that fire was. Ukrainian president Zelensky accuses Russia of a drone attack on a Turkish ship that was carrying corn. Since the start of the war between Ukraine and Russia four years ago, several European countries have had to deal with Russian drones violating their airspace, as well as with mines in the Black Sea on important trade and energy routes.

title: 3 years after Hamas terror attack, residents return, but the trauma remains
lead: Three years after the Hamas terror attack on 7 October 2023, most residents have returned to their homes in the border region near Gaza. Of the 47 evacuated communities, at least 43 are officially inhabited again. But although the residents are picking up life again, the wounds have not yet healed. "Both adults and children still have difficulty falling asleep at night," says Sharon Ofri. She lives in kibbutz Kissufim. "Our loved ones are buried here, how are you supposed to deal with that," she wonders. The residents of kibbutz Kissufim were evacuated to hotels by the Dead Sea and later stayed in Omer near the city of Beersheba in southern Israel. Ofri returned with her family last year as one of the few. Most residents have been living in the kibbutz again since this summer. Before 7 October 2023, some 62,000 people lived in the border region near Gaza. The region is said to have since attracted some 5,000 additional residents. Israel aims to reach a population of 124,000 in 2030. Like a film The memories of 7 October 2023 are still fresh for Sharon Ofri. "It was a mess, a real mess. Noise, screaming and gunshots everywhere," she says in her living room. "It hurts, it feels like a film when I think back on it." Around half past six in the morning, Hamas launches a large-scale attack on Israel. Thousands of rockets are fired and terrorists from Hamas and other armed groups cross the border and kill some 1,200 residents and soldiers. 251 people are also kidnapped and taken to Gaza as hostages. Kibbutz Kissufim is also hit hard. Twenty residents are killed and the body of 85-year-old Shlomo Mantzur is taken to Gaza. Houses, schools and the dairy farm are destroyed and set on fire. A memorial space has been set up in the kibbutz with the photos of the killed residents: fourteen Israelis and six workers from Thailand. "This is about 10 percent of our community," says Shoshi Shaked. She is responsible for the reconstruction of the kibbutz. "It remains hard to comprehend, sometimes it feels as if I am still waiting to wake up from a very long nightmare." According to Shaked, some 97 percent of the buildings in the kibbutz were severely damaged. The Israeli government has budgeted approximately 5 billion euros for the reconstruction and development of the Gaza border region, a programme that runs until 2028. Yet Shaked does not feel that the government has done enough. "Every community ultimately had to raise money itself, which means that not enough money came from the state." In the meantime, virtually everything in Kissufim has been renovated and rebuilt. But according to Shaked, the wounds have not healed with that. "Renovating buildings is simpler than repairing the human soul. You cannot simply replace that, it is a long and complicated process." Fear of Hamas Sharon Ofri is also still fully in the recovery process. "We still live daily with the traumas of 7 October 2023, it is a great challenge. Nobody understands it, only those who experienced it. That is why we try to hold on to each other and help, that is the only thing that works." Moreover, she lives daily with the fear that an attack like that of 7 October 2023 could repeat itself. "In images from Gaza we see that Hamas is still arming itself. We are startled by every bang we hear. At every hole in the border fence I think: What is going on? Is there a new infiltration?" When you walk out the front door at Ofri's, you look out on Gaza, on the city of Deir al-Balah. "It is a few kilometres further on," she says as we walk to the gate of the kibbutz. Occasionally army vehicles drive past. "I do not have the feeling of safety here," she says. Yet she does not think of living anywhere else. "This is my home. Just as there are people who want to live in Tel Aviv, we live here. This is home." On the other side of the border live Palestinians who also still live daily in fear because of the Israeli bombardments. But Ofri is not occupied with that at the moment, she says. "I am now busy with our recovery, the recovery of my community. That is what it is about for me now, not about them."

title: Nobel Prize in Physics goes to research on 'ghostly messengers from the cosmos'
lead: The Nobel Prize in Physics this year goes to the scientist Francis Halzen (82). He is the founder of the measurement of neutrinos, particles from the universe that contain an extreme amount of energy. The scientist, born in Belgium, is affiliated with the University of Wisconsin-Madison in the United States. From the 1980s onwards, Halzen conducted research into measuring neutrinos from the South Pole. He contributed to the Amanda detector. Later he helped build an even larger detector. This measuring instrument, named the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, was completed in 2010. On awarding the prize, the Swedish Nobel Committee spoke of "ghostly messengers from the cosmos". "Francis Halzen has led an international team of researchers and engineers that has provided us with a fantastic instrument. His persistence and scientific vision have paved the way for a new kind of astronomy." Halzen receives 12 million Swedish kronor. converted, approximately one million euros. It does not often happen that one scientist receives the full prize amount. Often the prize goes to a team of scientists that must share the amount together. Prizes increased Throughout the week it will be announced who will receive the Nobel Prizes this year. They will be awarded on 10 December, the day of death of namesake Nobel. Yesterday it was already announced that the Nobel Prize in Medicine will go to the American Karl Deisseroth and the Germans Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. They were awarded the prize for their discoveries in the field of optogenetics. This is an advanced technique with which nerve cells can be switched on and off with light. The Nobel Prizes were first awarded in1901. The prizes are paid from the estate of Alfred Nobel, who left 31 million kronor. The prize amount was adjusted several times over the past century. This year the amount was increased because of the 125th anniversary of the prize.

title: Injuries in air strikes on Saudi airports
lead: Two airports in Saudi Arabia have been attacked. At least three people were injured. The attacks have been claimed by the Houthis in neighbouring Yemen. The group says several missiles and drones were fired at Saudi Arabia. The attacks target the international airports of Jizan and Najran. Both cities are in the border area with Yemen. In addition to the injured, there was also material damage at the airports. The head of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf, in which Saudi Arabia sits together with five countries, speaks of a dangerous escalation. He calls the attacks unacceptable. The Houthis also claim to have carried out attacks on Abha airport, some 120 kilometres from the border. Saudi Arabia has not responded to that. A bloody civil war has been raging in Yemen for years. In recent years it was somewhat more stable there after a ceasefire was signed, but since July the Houthis have been engaged in a major advance. Where the Iran-backed group initially occupied only the northwest, in recent weeks they have conquered a number of strategic cities from the Yemeni government army, which is supported by Saudi Arabia. They also quickly gained control of the important Bab al-Mandab strait in the Red Sea. This is crucial for international shipping. The government army announced yesterday a large-scale operation that must stop the advance of the Houthis. It claims among other things to have regained control of the Bab al-Mandab strait. Also today the government army says it has recaptured several strategic positions from the Houthis. The fighting in the area is said to be becoming more intense. The government troops are being helped by the Saudi army, which is carrying out heavy air strikes.

title: 'Swimming lessons for children with disabilities must be more accessible'
lead: For children with a disability, swimming lessons are not always a given, especially not if their parents have money worries. Municipal income support for these parents falls short, says the Mulier Instituut, which conducted research into it. Swimming lessons for children with a disability are often more expensive than regular swimming lessons. The research shows that children benefit from smaller groups of four or two pupils and sometimes even one-on-one lessons. "That is so that they have less distraction from other children and that they get more attention from their teacher," explains researcher Mirjam Stuij of the Mulier Instituut. A swimming instructor must also know how to deal with a child with a disability. These two factors make the adapted swimming lessons more expensive. "That is difficult for parents, but also for swimming instructors." Existing schemes fall short Municipalities already offer schemes and allowances, but these are sometimes unclear and differ per municipality. Parents run into several things when applying, explains Stuij. "For example, the reimbursement they receive does not cover the cost of the swimming lesson." There are also parents who formally have too high an income for the schemes, but because of high healthcare costs or other high costs due to the child's disability, still have money worries. So they do not qualify. As a third point, the institute sees that applying for schemes can ask a lot of parents. That is because information from the municipality is unclear or because parents do not know where to turn. Fewer or no diplomas Stuij emphasises that parents consider a swimming diploma of great importance. "If my child falls into a ditch I want him to be able to save himself. I think we can very well imagine that in the Netherlands." Figures from <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> show that 14 percent of children living in poverty have a disability, against 8 percent of children who do not live in poverty. Figures from Mulier also show that children with a disability obtain a swimming diploma at a later age, obtain fewer diplomas or no swimming diploma. Clarity and flexibility The institute advises municipalities to map out how it is arranged with them, what the municipality reimburses and for whom. "Because we know that that varies enormously," says Stuij. The research results in a number of recommendations for local authorities. For example, there should be good information provision for parents and the application process must be made as clear as possible. The institute advocates more flexibility in income support. For example a standard reimbursement that can be increased if the costs for a child are higher, Stuij explains. The institute also advises establishing a fixed point of contact for parents. "Someone who can help them with the application and for example with finding suitable swimming lessons."

title: Fashion site Asos possibly hacked, customers receive strange notification
lead: The British fashion site Asos has possibly been hacked. Users of the app received a cryptic notification on their phone this morning, from which it can be concluded that the clothing company has been hacked. On social media customers are sharing screenshots of the notification. The message is addressed to Asos's security team. "We have the Snowflake environment completely under our control", the text reads. Snowflake develops software for companies and also offers a service for storing and analysing data. Among others, the British newspaper The Independent writes about the possible hack. According to the newspaper, it is not yet clear how many customers received the message. Asos has 17 million customers worldwide spread across more than 150 countries. In 2025 the company had a turnover of 2.5 billion British pounds, converted about 3 billion euros. The company's share price plunged by more than 10 percent this morning. Asos, which is also popular in the Netherlands, has itself not yet said anything about a possible hack. Earlier hacks Yesterday another major hack also took place. Hackers managed to obtain data from Denmark's population register. The hackers got hold of, among other things, the names and addresses of some 8.8 million Danes. The hackers also managed to steal the Danish version of the citizen service number (bsn). Last week grocery deliverer Flink was hacked. The hackers asked not only the company for payments, but also individual customers. No one responded to that; NOS previously spoke with experts who say that people are looking at data leaks with increasing indifference.

title: School cancels trip to France due to violence around pupil protests
lead: A secondary school in Oud-Beijerland cancelled a trip to France at the last moment due to unrest in that country, broadcaster Rijnmond writes. The pupils will instead go to Drenthe this week. The vwo pupils of two classes were supposed to leave yesterday and stay for a week with host families in the town of Mantes-la-Jolie, near Paris. These are pupils who follow bilingual education. In France, protests have been held since the end of September against problems in secondary education, such as overcrowded classes, a shortage of teachers and high work pressure. Those protests sometimes ended in violent confrontations with the police. Dozens of people were injured around the protests and thousands of demonstrators were arrested. Yesterday a 15-year-old pupil lost his hand at a protest in Lens after a flash grenade exploded. In Mantes-la-Jolie things remained calm last week. That is why the school trip initially seemed to go ahead as normal, says vice-principal Nicole van Leenen. "Of course we also saw the images on television. But we were told that it was not too bad there. But during Thursday that began to change and some unrest was expected for this week." Understanding Parents and pupils responded with understanding to the decision, according to the vice-principal. Many pupils were themselves in contact with peers at the French sister school in Mantes-la-Jolie and were therefore aware of the situation. Other pupils of the school are going on trips to England, Prague or Berlin. Precisely for that reason the school still wanted to arrange an alternative for the pupils who would go to France. "It is quite something different: Prague or Drenthe, but there is still understanding for it and we will make it a nice outing."

title: AfD member elected parliamentary president, step in takeover of power in Saxony-Anhalt
lead: The AfD has for the first time gained the presidency of a state parliament. At the first session of the newly elected parliament in Saxony-Anhalt, AfD member Tobias Rausch was elected. It marks an important milestone in the takeover of power in the state. AfD leader Ulrich Siegmund speaks of a historic day. The left-wing opposition also uses big words. For the first time since Hermann Göring, an extreme-right parliamentary president has been elected in Germany, was heard from Die Linke, SPD and the Greens. The AfD in Saxony-Anhalt has been labelled extreme-right by the security service. The AfD won last month's state election in Saxony-Anhalt with nearly 44 percent. Rausch was elected with more yes votes than expected. These involve the five votes of the small populist party BSW, which is open to cooperation with the AfD, and another four votes, presumably from co-voters from the CDU. This outcome offers the AfD good hope that forming an AfD government is likewise possible. Changes on the way The role of parliamentary president is a prominent position in terms of standing. As highest representative, in protocol he even ranks above the government leader in Saxony-Anhalt. He decides who may or may not enter the parliament, from press to speakers, and can appoint and replace officials. The first symbolic change already became visible today. The AfD group will henceforth sit in the middle of the parliament, while the left-wing opposition is divided over the left and right flanks. A far-reaching measure that is feared is the adjustment of the committees in which legislation is prepared. The AfD could adjust this composition so that the party occupies half of the seats. In that way the party can set the agenda and obstruct unwelcome legislation. The AfD can now show how the party wants to govern: radically and authoritarianly, or precisely professionally and moderately. In his word of thanks, Rausch took a constitutional stance and promised to place himself above the party. "Employees need not be afraid, as long as someone does his work normally," he previously told Tagesspiegel . In this way the AfD can show that it is possible to govern with the party, in order to convince other parties to form a coalition, both now and in the longer term. Nationally too, the AfD is by far polled as the largest and the party hopes to be able to lead the next federal government. Rausch is considered moderate. The 35-year-old former estate agent has long belonged to the circle around Siegmund. This spring he was accused of nepotism: family members turned out to work for him, as did players of the football club of which he is chairman. Where consequences were drawn with other AfD members , Rausch went unpunished. Government formation According to AfD leader Siegmund, today the "childish" Brandmauer was broken into pieces. That is the agreement of other parties not to cooperate with the AfD in any way. According to Siegmund, several talks are underway to have him appointed premier in December. BSW sticks to the proposal to elect an impartial government leader. The left-wing parties were prepared to discuss this, but the CDU rejects the idea. That party accepts an AfD government and wants to adopt a 'constructive' stance from the opposition. Officially, only talks with the BSW have been held so far. That party remains critical of the AfD at the same time. For instance, there was recently indignation about remarks by Siegmund about investments in defence companies. According to him, these are needed as an "aid for remigration". "With that the AfD shows that it does not want to govern and is desperately seeking a way out through provocation," responded BSW chair De Masi. Defectors Siegmund also seems to hope for defectors in the CDU, which is internally divided after the historic defeat. Current state premier Schulze was recently elected group leader with a minimal majority of one vote. The party has a conservative flank, which earlier called for cooperation with the AfD. That flank appears to have voted for the AfD member today. Siegmund shows himself full of self-confidence in any case. As far as he is concerned, parts of his controversial government plans can also be implemented without a majority, such as the asylum plans. "For many plans you do not need the parliament at all," he said yesterday with conviction. Invalid election result? The left-wing parties suspect the AfD of having misused money in Saxony-Anhalt for its election campaign. The party is said to have used budget intended for parliamentary work for campaign purposes. According to jurists, it must therefore be investigated whether the elections were conducted fairly. If that is not the case, the elections may possibly have to be redone.

title: Event organisations in Breda write urgent letter about higher permit costs
lead: Eighteen event organisations in Breda, such as Breda Jazz, Ploegendienst and carnival activities, have jointly sent an urgent letter to the city council. They demand more openness about the announced price increases for event permits, writes Omroep Brabant . From 2027, the municipality will increase the costs for an event permit. For example, the cost of a permit for large events, such as the large carnival parade, will rise from 17,000 euros to nearly 37,000 euros. For smaller events, the rate doubles from 4900 to more than 10,000 euros. 'It is not going to happen' The organisations fear that the higher costs will be the death knell for some events. Stichting Kielegat, a volunteer organisation for carnival activities in the city, says it cannot afford the price increase. "I see no possibility at all of raising that amount extra within a year. It is simply not going to happen," said chairman Rutger Westenburg after the announcement . Breda Jazz Festival attracts around 250,000 visitors annually. Nevertheless, the price increase also came as a shock to chairwoman Hanneke Griffioen. "It is a substantial amount, so you do blink your eyes at that and then you think: am I reading this correctly?" She therefore wants to sit down with the municipality. "Because this is not a normal price increase." The municipality says the higher costs are necessary because Breda has for years passed on only about twenty percent of the costs surrounding permit applications. "We have tried to keep the increase limited, but unfortunately... Everything is becoming more expensive," says responsible alderman Arjen van Drunen. Even after the increase, according to Van Drunen, the full costs are still not covered. Transparency Among the signatories of the letter are volunteer organisations, but also commercial organisers. Koninklijke Horeca Nederland Breda and organised hospitality entrepreneurs have also joined. "With all these organisations, we mainly want transparency about how these permit fees are built up," says Johan de Vos of Koninklijke Horeca Nederland Breda. "We want to see what the substantiation is. That this is a broadly supported request is clear from all the organisations that have lined up behind this letter." The organisers demand insight into the full calculation behind the new rates. They want to know how many civil service hours are charged, which hourly rates are passed on and whether costs for enforcement, public order and traffic measures are included in the rates. After that, they want to discuss with the municipality what part of the costs organisers must pay. According to them, it must be clear which costs really belong to the permit and which belong to the municipality's normal tasks. "The mere fact that certain activities take place around events does not automatically mean that these costs can be recovered from the individual organiser through event fees," they write. In addition, the event organisations also want to look at whether the permit process can be made cheaper.

title: First patient with Ebola virus in Kenya has died, man contracted virus in Congo
lead: In Kenya, a patient with the Ebola virus died yesterday for the first time. The Kenyan had contracted the virus in Congo, reports the Ministry of Health. Kenya is the fourth country to register an Ebola case. The man travelled back to Kenya via Uganda on Saturday and was placed in isolation in a hospital in the capital Nairobi after arrival. He tested positive for the Ebola virus after he developed fever and severe bleeding. The Kenyan authorities have started a source and contact investigation. The contacts, including 23 passengers who were on the same flight from Uganda, are in isolation until they test negative for the virus. Deadliest outbreak ever Ebola is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by a virus. It can be transmitted through bodily fluids such as blood, semen and vomit and causes bleeding in the body. Since the end of May there has officially been an Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo. The severe outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo variant of the virus and is considered the deadliest ever in the African country. There are still no vaccines or treatments against the disease. Attempts to bring the disease under control are difficult So far, more than 8000 people in the country have been infected with the virus. More than 4000 people have died from the disease. In neighbouring country Uganda, 20 Ebola cases have been registered so far. In France, a case of Ebola has been confirmed.

title: Very heavy art book with work by Dalí stolen from French museum
lead: One of the most expensive and heaviest books in the world has been stolen from a museum in France. The cover of the artwork the Apocalypse, made by Salvador Dalí, alone weighs 150 kilos. It is a mystery how the thieves got the lead-heavy book out of the building. The Public Prosecution Service has started an investigation into the theft in the municipality of Issoire, about a hundred kilometres west of Lyon. The police have not released any details about the art theft in the night from Sunday to Monday. It is unclear whether there are any suspects. 'Murder of heritage' The owner of the artwork calls the theft an attack on the French cultural sector. "France was murdered last night. French heritage was murdered," Christian Karoutzos said to French media yesterday evening. The Apocalypse was made between 1958 and 1961 and weighs about 210 kilos in total. Fourteen of the most renowned artists of that time contributed to the project. The famous Spanish painter Dalí made the bronze cover. Dalí was one of the best-known artists of the last century. He painted surrealist works and was an eccentric person. He wore a distinctive thin moustache, with the tips curled upwards. The moustache is "the most serious part of my personality", Dalí once said jokingly in an interview.

title: Passenger ship near Zeeland stuck on sandbank, occupants evacuated
lead: Along the coast near Zeeuws-Vlaanderen, a passenger ship with 75 occupants has run aground on a sandbank. Almost all people on board have now been evacuated. A spokesperson for the Dutch Coastguard confirms this to the NOS. The evacuated passengers have been brought to Breskens. According to the coastguard, many of them are elderly. This was taken into account during the rescue operation. The Coastguard speaks of a "major rescue operation". "We sent our helicopter and rescue boats out. The helicopter ultimately turned out not to be needed," a spokesperson says. The ship is still stuck on the sandbank near Breskens. Three crew members have remained on board. "It is good if there are people on board to maintain contact," a spokesperson says. How the ship ended up on the sandbank is not yet known. The passenger ship is about 100 years old.

title: Spanish Supreme Court withdraws arrest warrant for separatist leader Puigdemont
lead: The arrest warrant against Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont has been withdrawn by the Spanish Supreme Court. Puigdemont can thus, after having lived in exile for nine years, return to his country as a free man without being arrested. Puigdemont fled to Belgium in 2017, after Catalonia's attempt to secede from Spain failed. A referendum on secession was illegal according to the Spanish Supreme Court. In Brussels he eventually became a Member of the European Parliament in 2019. Puigdemont was also prosecuted for embezzling public money during the referendum. That is why the 2024 amnesty law initially did not apply to him, according to the court. The Spanish Constitutional Court ruled today that courts must apply the amnesty law to Catalan separatists even if there are cases pending about embezzlement. Referendum Catalonia declared itself unilaterally independent from Spain in 2017, after an illegal referendum. Puigdemont was at that time the government leader of Catalonia. The vote was ultimately boycotted by the Catalans who wanted to remain with Spain, so that ultimately 90 percent of Catalans voted for independence. Madrid decided to intervene after the referendum, after which Puigdemont fled the country. A number of his ministers stayed and were sentenced to prison terms of up to 13 years. Most of them later received a pardon from the government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Arrest warrant Spain issued an arrest warrant against Puigdemont several times, both nationally and European. In 2018 he was arrested in Germany and was released after thirteen days. Three years later he was temporarily detained on Sardinia. However, he was never extradited to Spain. Two years ago, the 63-year-old Puigdemont returned to Catalonia very briefly. In Barcelona he gave a speech. Although hundreds of officers were deployed and several roads were closed, the politician ultimately managed to leave Spain again. The withdrawal of the arrest warrant comes at a politically sensitive moment in Spain. The country goes to the polls early on 29 November. Puigdemont's party, Junts, is currently low in the polls.

title: Cat theft gang in Vietnam busted: 'Thousands of animals stolen'
lead: The Vietnamese <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has busted a network responsible for the theft of thousands of cats in Ho Chi Minh City. Twelve men are suspected of stealing and reselling the animals, presumably for consumption, state media report. The main suspect is 39-year-old Luu Thanh Binh, he is the suspected gang leader. According to the police investigation, Binh bought live cats, and kept the cats at a location in the city to then resell them. Under him worked several people who in turn recruited others to steal cats in different parts of the city. The network consisted of small groups each with their own area. At night the groups went through residential neighborhoods on motorbikes looking for cats. They made their own cat traps. According to the suspects, each group stole four to ten cats per night. 50 cats rescued The police carried out a raid in the Dong Thanh district in July. 50 cats were rescued in the process. Dozens of cat traps, scales, mobile phones, motorbikes, grooming devices and cash were also seized. Of the 50 rescued cats, thirteen have now been reunited with their owners, the other owners are still being sought. The suspects are said to have admitted during their interrogation to having stolen a total of 2700 cats. It is not known exactly how long the gang was active. During an earlier raid in June, 400 cats were rescued. The animals were locked in 45 cages. During that raid, more than 80 dead cats were also found that were being cooled with ice. Nine people were arrested. Eating cats and dogs Eating cats and dogs is not illegal in Vietnam, provided the sellers have the correct permits. The police emphasize that knowingly and deliberately buying illegal meat is punishable, as is the trade in stolen animals. There are no official figures on the local consumption of dogs and cats, but resistance to it has been growing in recent years in Vietnam. Especially among young people and pet owners, writes animal welfare organization Humane World for Animals. They point to the cruelty and animal abuse involved in the illegal capture, trade, storage and transport of the animals. But there is also increasing resistance because cats and dogs are increasingly seen as companion animals and not as food.

title: Online trade in 'extortion packages' of women, Belgium and the Netherlands investigate
lead: <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> (VVD) of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> is going to ask the Dutch <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> to offer help to the Belgian police, which is investigating the trading of nude photos of women on the so-called darkweb. He said this in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> where he was asked questions about the case, which RTL reported on. Nude photos and private data of hundreds of Belgian and Dutch women are being traded on the hidden part of the internet, RTL reported. Ready-made packages with intimate photos, social media profiles and contact details are offered on a site that has been active since 2023. Women can be harassed and extorted with them. For one euro per victim, access is provided to private data and photos. The 'packages' are sold to multiple people at once. The website offers to remove data from the platform for a payment of 250 euros, but it is unclear whether this actually happens. 'Perverse practices' There is great aversion across the Kamer. Minister Van Weel spoke of horrific practices of a "perversity that you do not often see". He also expressed his sympathy with the victims. One of the victims is a 31-year-old woman from Limburg who told her story to RTL. She had panic attacks when she heard that she was on the site. Fifteen years later, her photos are still surfacing. Van Weel called her story shocking and believes she is doing fantastic work by, among other things, removing the shame among victims. Kamer members want justice to act firmly, if necessary at European level. "This is organized sexual violence," says VVD Kamer member Becker. "These are not incidents, but a revenue model," says Pro Kamer member Mutluer. The Kamer wants the site to go offline as soon as possible. The parties also want the Dutch <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> to be involved in the case quickly. 'Investigation difficult' What is happening here is punishable but investigation will not be easy, says Van Weel. "It is technically not simple to find out who is behind what on the darkweb, where the server is, how a site can be taken offline". Van Weel says that he "cannot shut down the darkweb tomorrow with a bill". According to him, there are possibilities to take sites offline, but then "first very technical specific investigations are needed, and we will certainly deploy on that". The Belgian police have announced an investigation and Van Weel is going to ask the Dutch police "to consult the Antwerp police and see how we can help". The Dutch Openbaar Ministerie is not yet investigating the case, a spokesperson told the NOS, but the OM does not rule out that it will later join an international joint investigation . "Given the facts and the number of potential Dutch victims, it would be logical if a request for help comes from Belgium, then we are also prepared to help." Can you look up whether your data has been leaked? For those who are concerned by this news or whether their data or photos can be found on the darkweb, there is unfortunately no satisfactory answer: there is currently no simple way to search for that, a spokesperson for knowledge center Offlimits told the NOS. "We do not recommend that people search for their name or images on the darkweb themselves. In our view, there is no public and safe way to check that yourself on the darkweb." Moreover, she warns: "You do not know what you will encounter there. In this kind of environment there can also be other illegal or very shocking material. You also have no control over what appears on a page. Moreover, searching yourself does not provide certainty about whether or not you appear on the website. If you do not find your name, that does not automatically mean that you are not in the database. And conversely, a namesake can of course cause confusion. You may also be able to disrupt a police investigation with this." Her tip is: "Do you have concerns or concrete indications that your images or data have been shared, for example because someone approaches or threatens you with this? Then contact Offlimits or the police. Together we can look at what is going on and what steps you can take."

title: Adults predominantly positive about LGBTI people, well-being of some groups 'concerning'
lead: Broadly speaking, the views of adult Dutch people on, for example, homosexuality are unchanged compared with two years ago. There are, however, large differences between the individual LGBTI+ groups. Moreover, the well-being of the groups varies greatly. This emerges from the biennial Lhbtiqa+monitor by Movisie, Panteia and Ipsos I&O. In September, another study revealed that acceptance of homosexuality among young people has declined over the past four years. That study was conducted among young people between the ages of 12 and 16. Who is this study about? The Lhbtiqa+monitor is a study carried out every two years on behalf of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. The abbreviation stands for the groups the study is about: lesbian, homosexual, bisexual, transgender, intersex, queer, asexual and non-binary persons. Not only their living situation is addressed. Every two years the researchers also ask about Dutch people's views on these groups. Although homosexuality is still predominantly viewed positively (84 percent), a slight shift is visible. Compared with two years ago, slightly more respondents think 'neutrally' about this group instead of 'positively'. The share of respondents who judge homosexuality negatively has remained stable (4 percent). Views on other groups have also remained broadly the same when compared with two years ago. The fact that little has changed in general is considered concerning by researcher Karijn van den Berg of Movisie. "Views on, for example, homosexuality are generally positive, but that applies much less to intersex, transgender and non-binary persons," the researcher said. When you zoom in on groups, changes are indeed visible. For instance, 65 percent of those surveyed found sex between two men "not disgusting" in 2024, while that number has now fallen to 60 percent. Moreover, more than a quarter of respondents have "difficulty with" kissing in public, mainly when it concerns two men. Two years ago that applied to about a fifth of Dutch people. Gender or sexual identity as a 'fashion phenomenon' The study also shows that being transgender, non-binary and bisexual is relatively often seen as a fashion phenomenon by those surveyed. That concerns the researchers. They also find it concerning that many respondents do not want a relationship with transgender, non-binary, bisexual, asexual or intersex persons. Another conclusion of the researchers is the limited knowledge about asexual, non-binary and intersex persons. Many questions about these groups are not answered by the respondents. They often indicate not knowing the answer or never having thought about it. "This finding shows that the knowledge about and understanding, or recognition, of these groups of persons in Dutch society is still fairly limited," the report states. The researchers did not only look at Dutch people's views on the individual LGBTI+ groups. They also mapped the well-being of those groups themselves. There too the differences between the groups are large, the report shows. Well-being of LGBTI+ persons Where the living situation of homosexual persons is generally comparable to that of heterosexuals, that of intersex, transgender and non-binary persons can be called concerning, the report states. For instance, they more often deal with depression, suicidal thoughts, financial problems and discrimination, a survey among these groups shows. Researcher Van den Berg calls these large differences in well-being between the studied groups "very striking". "We see a real gap between, for example, homosexual and transgender people, both in terms of acceptance and in terms of well-being." The researchers make a number of recommendations to the cabinet. For instance, they advise education and information about sexual and gender diversity. They also recommend paying attention to online hate and disinformation about LGBTI+ persons in lessons about media literacy. Attention to the studied groups in vocational training programmes in care and welfare and more room for inclusive policy in government are other recommendations. The groups the study is about Lesbian persons: women who are attracted to women. Homosexual persons: men who are attracted to men. Bi+ persons: persons who are attracted to more than one gender. Transgender persons: people whose gender identity does not (fully) correspond with the sex assigned at birth. Non-binary persons: people who identify as non-binary, feel at home with a gender identity outside the (binary) categories of man and woman. Intersex persons: are born with a body that does not correspond with the image most people have of man or woman. Queer persons: people who cannot find themselves in the usual, fixed (binary) frameworks and boxes for gender and/or sexual orientation, or reject these frameworks. Asexual persons: people who experience no or little sexual attraction to other persons.

title: IND must get to work on 140,000 applications from Ukrainians, asylum system further under pressure
lead: The asylum applications of more than 140,000 Ukrainians that have been put on the shelf must still be looked at and assessed. This appears from a ruling by the European Court of Justice. Among administrators it is now beginning to sink in that this can have major consequences for the pressure on the asylum chain, can be heard from those involved. <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> also admits that it has a problem. Ukrainians who came to the Netherlands because of the war fell under the Temporary Protection Directive. With this rule devised from Europe, displaced persons can receive temporary protection. The Netherlands has only arranged this in such a way that when you want to receive that protection, you also had to submit an asylum application. That application was then automatically suspended. And parking those asylum applications, as it were, is not allowed, the European court ruled last week. "We long chose not to process applications from Ukrainians in the Netherlands, because of the fact that they already received protection," says responsible Minister Van den Brink of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>. "Also because it was a very large number. The court now says clearly: that must be done," says the minister. Extra pressure on the asylum chain Asylum lawyer Wil Eikelboom: "In hindsight it was not such a good idea to link temporary protection to submitting an asylum application. Very clumsy." In other countries, an asylum application was not automatically submitted if someone fell under the Temporary Protection Directive. "The Netherlands is really an exception in that," says Ricky van Oers, assistant professor of Sociology of Law and Migration Law at Radboud University. So all applications from Ukrainians must now be processed. "The question is how the IND is going to do this, they actually have no capacity for it at all," says Eikelboom. The minister admits that this ruling of the court will "certainly" put extra pressure on the asylum system. "At the same time, the court also offers room," says the minister, who thus hopes to make his problem manageable. He interprets the ruling in such a way that he does not have to process the application of all Ukrainians immediately. Van den Brink wants to first process the asylum applications of people who are arriving now, then and at the same time the more than fifty thousand people who were already on the waiting list and only after that give priority to this group of Ukrainians. In short: yes, the asylum application of the Ukrainians must be processed but the minister wants to wait for the time being with most of them. According to assistant professor of migration law Van Oers, there are indeed nuances in the ruling of the European Court. "Because it concerns so many applications, the Netherlands may possibly process the procedures in phases. They can also decide that they give priority to certain groups, for example, think of families." But the question is how much room the minister's approach will really yield, because all this will in any case mean extra work. 'Permanent temporariness' The advantage of that directive for Ukrainians was, for example, that they were allowed to work here immediately - in contrast to asylum seekers. It also gives temporary entitlement to shelter, medical care and education for children. But that also brings uncertainty with it. "Ukrainians live here in permanent temporariness," says Van Oers. "Because of that temporary protection there is continuously little prospect of building a life. While in fact there is an asylum application. Such an asylum status gives more certainty." The temporary protection of Ukrainians now runs until March 2028. It is still unclear whether it will be extended after that. According to Vluchtelingenwerk, the ruling of the European Court of Justice has probably not yet reached many Ukrainians. "But it undoubtedly leads to more unrest and uncertainty. Return to Ukraine is at this moment not a realistic option." Vluchtelingenwerk wants a sustainable plan for Ukrainians in the Netherlands. "With a quick and careful assessment of their residence permit so that these people, who have already been through a great deal, know where they stand." The highest administrative court in the Netherlands must now assess the European ruling. After that it will become clear what its meaning is in practice. According to lawyers, the Netherlands can in any case not ignore the ruling.

title: Podcast De Dag: what makes the French school protests increasingly bigger
lead: The French school protest is becoming bigger, more violent and more political. Today, during a national day of protest, at least tens of thousands, according to the union even hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets, in solidarity with the French school students. The protest erupted two weeks ago, at the start of the school year. It concerns a shortage of teachers, inadequate lesson schedules and materials. And inequality: schools in the banlieues are hit much harder than schools in other places. Listen? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Enjoying it? Then do not forget to subscribe. In the podcast De Dag, Dutch students Raoul and Felix, who are studying in France, tell what they see happening around them and what moves their fellow students. Niek Pas is a France expert at the UvA and previously also taught in France. According to him, we must also see the protests in the light of the upcoming presidential elections. Politicians jump on the unrest and point fingers at each other about the causes of the poor state of education. Respond? Mail dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial staff: Max Smedes and Wouter Sloekers Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: New suspect arrested in London for preparing attack at air force base
lead: In London a new suspect has been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist attack at the air force base in Fairford. That is reported by the counter-terrorism department of the British police. It concerns a 22-year-old man with British nationality. A home has also been searched in the same area. On 27 September the alarm was raised at a British air force base in the county of Gloucestershire, after suspicious white vans had been spotted. The police feared that there were explosives in the white vans and homes were evacuated as a precaution. Only cans of petrol were found in the vans. On that same day five British men were arrested. Later it turned out that one of the suspects had earlier called the police himself . On 1 October another suspect was picked up. The six suspects are all in their twenties. They may await further investigation at liberty. Bombers removed At the Royal Air Force air force base near Fairford, besides British soldiers, American soldiers and bombers that are active in the war against Iran are also stationed. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps earlier let it be known that every base involved in the war is considered a legitimate target. The US therefore points to Iran as the guilty party, but Iran itself denies being involved. On Sunday the US removed all twelve bombers from the air force base. That would have happened because of a new threat that according to American media comes from Iran.

title: ChatGPT texts also get an invisible 'watermark'
lead: Texts from ChatGPT users are being provided with an invisible 'watermark'. This should make clearer whether a text is authentic or generated by artificial intelligence, according to OpenAI. The watermark, called textGrain, will be incorporated in the coming period into AI texts from users in the European Union. Outside that, the texts contain no watermarks. The recognition mark is not visible to normal users: it is namely not a physical stamp or special character, but is built into the word choices of the generative AI model. Short texts A special detector can pick up that watermark, and thereby AI-generated words and texts. That tool is for now only accessible to approved researchers and expert organisations, OpenAI writes. According to the company behind ChatGPT, the system is strong, but not flawless, the company writes. Among other things, short and edited texts make reliable detection difficult. Anthropic, the company behind chatbot Claude, introduced a comparable watermark two months ago: also invisible to human eyes, but observable to computer systems. This one has been applied worldwide. Competition The companies say that with their watermarks they are following the new European AI transparency rules. One of those rules is that content made by artificial intelligence gets a marking, such as a watermark. According to tech expert Bert Hubert, in Europe you may still make texts produced by artificial intelligence without a watermark, but then under some circumstances you must state it yourself. According to Hubert, the fact that the companies are now adding watermarks en masse is therefore due to mutual competition. "Otherwise, as OpenAI, you would now almost have to explain why as a company you do not have this. Something like that can be bad for your sales process." Fraud cases The watermarks come at a time when there is much discussion about the authenticity of content and what the consequences are if content is not authentic. "This raises the bar somewhat," says Hubert. According to him, the watermarks can especially help in fraud cases. "Think of emails from a supposed energy company that look credible, but were produced by artificial intelligence. Then it is very useful if your email system can say: watch out, this is an AI-generated email."

title: Free ice cream promotion gets out of hand, police intervene
lead: A promotion in which an ice cream parlour gave away free ice creams in Almere got out of hand yesterday. The many young people present became so annoying that the business had to close its doors on the advice of the police. "We wanted to do something good for the neighbourhood and then you get this," the owner says to Omroep Flevoland . The free ice cream promotion reached many young people. On TikTok the announcement was viewed more than 130,000 times. According to the entrepreneur, the first hour went smoothly, but after that the atmosphere turned. Sent away According to the owner, there was pushing and shoving and young people harassed employees. "We almost had to work as bodyguards instead of as ordinary employees." Eventually the police were called. According to the entrepreneur, several vehicles came to the scene and officers went into the business with a police dog. A police spokesperson says that the young people were sent away, but that no one was arrested. The owner is disappointed. "We wanted to bring people together and organise something fun. But of course our staff must be able to work safely."

title: EU enlargement open for discussion again, but first a trial period for new countries
lead: For years the subject was undiscussable in Brussels: admitting new countries to the European Union. The last accession, that of Croatia, dates back to 2013. The fear is that new countries will mainly cost money. Moreover, there are concerns about the stability of newcomers. Will they continue to abide by the European rules once they are members? But since the war in Ukraine and the re-election of Donald Trump, support for new members is growing.
