"A larger European Union gives us more political and economic weight in a world full of fierce competition on the world stage," says European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos. The idea is that you stand stronger together. For example, due to the war the Ukrainian army is the strongest in Europe and EU countries can learn a lot from it. It must also be prevented that Russia or China gains more influence over countries in Europe. Taking away voting rights The European Commission is therefore today coming with a plan for new rules for newcomers. The rules must ensure that acceding countries actually make the EU stronger and not weaker. For instance, the Commission wants extra rules to be able to punish new countries if they do not abide by the basic principles of the EU after their accession. If they do violate those principles concerning, for example, democracy, the rule of law or human rights within the first fifteen years as a new member, then voting rights can be taken away. Four direct candidates Especially Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine are currently on course for EU membership. The small Montenegro (600,000 inhabitants) wants to become the 28th member of the EU in 2028 and is well on schedule. The proposal contains not only ideas to monitor new countries, but also to keep a larger EU governable. If even more countries join, it becomes more difficult to reach agreements that all countries agree on. The Commission therefore advocates taking decisions by majority more often. That must consist of 55 percent of the countries in which together more than 65 percent of the EU population lives. Now, for many important decisions, the support of all EU countries is needed. That regularly leads to difficult negotiations. A country can single-handedly block a proposal in the interest of only that country, as Greece, Luxembourg and France recently did with new sanctions against Russia. It is up to the EU countries themselves to decide whether they will take more decisions by majorities. The question is whether there is enough support for it. On the one hand it can make the EU more decisive, certainly with more members. On the other hand, countries can then exert less influence on their own. Ironically, all countries must agree if they decide to take decisions by majority in the future. Hungary The new rules must prevent a new 'Hungary scenario'. That country acceded to the European Union in 2004. Under Prime Minister Orbán, who governed from 2010 until this year, the rule of law subsequently declined. The independent judiciary came under great pressure, EU money was defrauded and Hungary ignored numerous European rules. The EU did take measures by freezing European subsidies for Hungary, but it did not succeed in taking away Hungary's voting rights. Legislation existed for that, but all EU countries had to support it and that did not happen. Poland, which likewise undermined the independent judiciary in the country, continued to support Hungary. That was also true the other way around. And so nothing happened for years, to the great dissatisfaction of the Netherlands, among others. Trojan Horse The plans that the Commission is now proposing must therefore make it easier to suspend the voting rights of future members during the first fifteen years of their membership. In this way the Commission hopes to avoid bringing in a 'Trojan Horse' from within. A country that at first sight seems a fine addition, but once inside the EU causes major problems. Next week the leaders of the EU countries will discuss the new enlargement plans at a European summit. Enlargement is a politically sensitive theme. The Netherlands has always been reticent, but does see something in these plans.

title: French PM: no lessons at French schools in coming days, talk with each other
lead: For the coming three days there will be no lessons at all lycées throughout France. That is what French Prime Minister Lecornu said. The reason is the large-scale pupil protests of recent weeks. Lycées are the upper years of secondary education, for pupils from around 15 years old. The Prime Minister wants, together with the Minister of Education, to give a political answer to the protests. He hopes that schools and pupils will enter into talks with each other in the coming days. Whether schools will heed this or whether schools want to let lessons continue is not clear. Lecornu calls the protests "real" and believes that the students must be listened to. He also mentioned a number of points of attention that the government can work on, such as the state of the school buildings. Also protests today Today too, tens of thousands of people took to the streets in French cities. It was the largest day of action since the protests began last month. Hundreds of schools were again closed. In the meantime, trade unions and parents have also thrown their support behind the protests. According to the Ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, at least 250,000 people are out today. One of the trade unions speaks of 450,000 demonstrators, even before the large demonstration in Paris began. Tens of thousands of people are also expected there during a march. In several places along the route the atmosphere is grim. Pupils and students demand more money for education. They are furious about the poor state of the school buildings and the teacher shortage. In several cities the police deployed tear gas. In Strasbourg, Lyon and Rennes, among others, fires were set by the demonstrators and objects were thrown at the police. According to Prime Minister Lecornu, 85 teachers and 215 pupils were injured in the protests of recent days. He calls it "the heaviest toll that education staff have suffered in decades". In the protests, 715 police officers were also injured.

title: No current travel information on digital boards at train stations due to malfunction
lead: The travel information system of NS has been dealing with a malfunction for some time. As a result, the current departure times could not be seen on the digital information boards. The travel information was not updated between approximately 17:00 and 18:15. An NS spokesperson says that not all digital boards or train stations were affected. In August there was also already a problem with the travel information system at NS. The IT system was dealing with an internal malfunction.

title: Three holiday parks of Peter Gillis sold for millions
lead: The sale of the three holiday parks of Peter Gillis that were auctioned last week will definitely go ahead. That is what auctioneer Richard Dieteren reports to Omroep Brabant . The creditor checked the bidders and no irregularities came to light in doing so. The holiday parks Prinsenmeer in Ommel, Brugse Heide in Valkenswaard and Stadsresort Valkenburg were forcibly auctioned because real estate entrepreneur Gillis has more than 27 million euros in debt with businessman Marc van Rooi. The man behind meat processing company Van Rooi Meat previously provided the millions loan to Gillis with his company M2R Invest in exchange for the mortgage right on the three parks. The sale of the three parks yields a total of 27.3 million euros. This does not yet free Gillis from his debts. There are still auction costs and another tax debt outstanding. Destination According to the auctioneer, the parks must be transferred to the new owners within six weeks. Who they are and when the new owners will open the parks is unknown. It is not certain whether all parks will remain designated for recreation. According to experts, the sale amount of Prinsenmeer is high for a holiday park and it may have been bought with a view to a different destination. For the hundreds of people with a chalet at Prinsenmeer, the coming weeks will be exciting: may they keep their holiday homes or will they go? National fame In holiday park Prinsenmeer, Gillis once started his business. Here the ins and outs of the entrepreneur and his family were also followed in the SBS series Massa is Kassa. With this reality series, Gillis gained national fame. In recent years, the entrepreneur mainly made the news because of tax fraud, domestic violence and debts. He still faces prison time, a millions fine and community service. Gillis now still has six closed holiday parks in the Netherlands and three 'open' parks in Belgium.

title: Again major protests and violence in France, what is behind it?
lead: France has been restless for a few weeks now. What started as a small-scale protest at a secondary school outside Paris has grown into a national popular movement that university students have also joined. At the same time, hooligans or rioters are abusing the demonstrations. Where does this unrest come from? Where in recent days it was still about hundreds of schools, demonstrators today blocked 1800 secondary schools. According to the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, at least 250,000 people were out, from Rennes and Toulouse to Paris, to further increase the pressure on the French government. Education and teacher unions are also taking part. The demonstrators want an end to a series of problems in French education, such as the poor state of the school buildings. The police act harshly: last week 5000 people were arrested, of whom 87 percent were minors. Pupils in a suburb of Paris decided on 17 September to block the entrance of their secondary school. They wanted to make a stand against overcrowded classes and long school days. The pupils did not stand alone; they received support from teachers who expressed their concerns about the shortage of staff and materials, and the high workload. French secondary school pupils are required to take more lesson hours than their peers in many other European countries. "I leave home at half past six in the morning and when I come back, it is seven o'clock in the evening. I see my teachers more often than my family. That is not normal," a pupil from Val-de-Marne says to local media. Vulnerable neighbourhoods In addition, many French secondary schools struggle with a shortage of basic provisions such as tables and chairs. Due to a lack of air conditioning, temperatures in classrooms rise considerably during heatwaves, while in winter it can be freezing cold. Pupils point to overdue maintenance, which leads to leaking roofs, cockroaches and rat infestations, as in Saint-Denis. According to activists, those problems are often greatest at schools in socioeconomically vulnerable neighbourhoods. Parcoursup, the platform with which pupils register for a follow-up study, is also under fire. Sometimes pupils have to wait months before they know whether they are admitted to their study of choice. According to many of them, the system causes uncertainty and extra stress about their future. Police violence The first demonstration was still fairly good-natured, with a few rubbish bins going up in flames. But via social media the images of it spread very quickly and protests spilled over to other cities outside Paris. The movement received support almost immediately from the radical-left party La France Insoumise (LFI), which has a strong following among young people. That support is not unimportant electorally, because some of the pupils will be allowed to vote for the first time in the French presidential elections next year. Right-wing politicians accuse the party of inciting and politicising the protest. For example, the LFI mayor of Saint-Denis, Bally Bagayoko, said that violence "is legitimised in some cases". Those words, which according to Bagayoko were taken out of context, led to much uproar. The centre-right presidential candidate Bruno Retailleau wondered whether LFI should not be banned. LFI leader Mélenchon instead states that his party only supports the movement and does not organise it. He wants the demonstrations to proceed without violence and points to what he describes as the "brutality" of the police. According to him, officers frequently used tear gas and batons to drive demonstrators apart. Yesterday in the French city of Lens a 15-year-old pupil lost his hand after he picked up a flash grenade that had been thrown by riot police. Almost 200 pupils and teachers have now been injured. Despite the disturbances, the demonstrators continue. Today it was thus about at least 250,000 people who took to the streets. According to one of the unions, there were even 450,000. On Sunday, Prime Minister Lecornu wrote a letter in which he promises to come with concrete commitments for pupils this week, among other things to make school buildings better resistant to the consequences of climate change. In addition, in the budget, which still has to be approved by parliament, 1.2 billion euros extra is being allocated for education. He also announced that at secondary schools no lessons will be given until Friday in the hope that schools and pupils will then enter into conversation with each other. But the fear is that the genie is now already out of the bottle and that the protest movement can grow into a much broader popular movement. That is also because there is much frustration in France about the high fuel prices. For example, the Yellow Vests movement, which largely paralysed France in 2018, has announced that it will take to the streets again on 17 October.

title: Disagreement over box 3: coalition divided over paper gifts
lead: The coalition is once again internally divided over the question of how the changes surrounding the wealth tax (box 3) should be paid for. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to tax wealthy people differently from 2028 and wants to introduce a so-called capital gains tax on savings, investments and a second home (box 3). A tax that is no longer levied annually on the growth of your assets, but only afterwards if, for example, you have sold shares. Parties consider that fairer for wealthy people. But changing the system will create a gap of billions in the budget in the coming years. D66 and CDA agree with a majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> that part of the gap can be closed by tackling the 'paper gift tax'. That is a fiscally favourable way to give money and thereby pay less inheritance tax. But the VVD does not want that to happen. "We are not going to touch that," says VVD <entity id="person:ruben-pieter-brekelmans">fractievoorzitter Brekelmans</entity> resolutely. Asked how things should proceed now, he says: "We will see, the cabinet will now get to work on it further." Seeking coverage During the Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen last week, great dissatisfaction arose about the way the cabinet wanted to cover the capital gains tax. The plan was to make a group of approximately 1.5 million investors with assets from 30,000 euros pay tax next year already. In addition, more savers and investors would pay wealth tax for the first time in the new system, which is due to take effect from 2028: from a profit above 1000 euros. So both plans did not go ahead. The cabinet then asked parties to come up with their own coverage proposals. Today the ChristenUnie came with the proposal to tackle paper gifts as coverage. That can count on a majority in the Kamer, but not on the undivided support of the coalition. 'Fed up with bickering' CDA <entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">leider Bontenbal</entity> thinks tackling the fiscal advantage of the paper gift tax is a good plan. The fact that the VVD thinks differently about it should be possible in a minority coalition, he says. What the outcome will now be "he does not know". The ChristenUnie is "fed up with the bickering after all these months". As far as ChristenUnie <entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">leider Bikker</entity> is concerned, the VVD must now go "from no to together". "You may really have a few sacred cows, but at a certain point the conversation must also follow." The VVD itself has another plan to close the gap in box 3: lowering the tax rate for entrepreneurs in box 2 even more than is currently in the plans. The idea is that entrepreneurs are thereby tempted to withdraw more money from their business. If more entrepreneurs do that, extra money temporarily flows into the treasury. The plan to go even further in that than the cabinet already wanted received a majority. In the long term, by the way, it is not enough to cover the transition to box 3. If the cabinet reaches agreement on the coverage of box 3, another problem still awaits. A Kamer majority is against the increase in income taxes that must yield 8 billion euros in the coming years. A majority from left to right calls on the cabinet to adjust those plans.

title: Paramount completes Warner Bros acquisition in giant deal of 111 billion dollars
lead: The acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery by media company Paramount Skydance has been finalised after more than a year. With the deal of 111 billion dollars (98 billion euros), a new media giant has been created. The company will be called Skydance. A little more than a year ago, Paramount Skydance made the first offer for Warner Bros, which had earlier already accepted a takeover offer from streaming service Netflix. Paramount and Netflix began a bidding battle, which led to the streaming service withdrawing . Too much power Twelve American states, led by California, filed a lawsuit in July to stop the billion-dollar takeover by Paramount. They feared that the company would gain too much power with the deal to raise prices for television and film consumers. At the end of last month, Paramount settled with the twelve states. The company made the promise to spend 300 million dollars more annually on film productions in the US and to release at least thirty films in American cinemas annually. Which channels and productions fall under Paramount and Warner Bros? Paramount owns, among others, television channels MTV and Nickelodeon and is co-owner of streaming service SkyShowtime. The company is also known for films such as Titanic and Gladiator and for film series such as Transformers , Mission: Impossible and Star Trek . Warner Bros owns the TV channels CNN, Eurosport, Cartoon Network and Discovery Channel. The company is also responsible for film series such as Harry Potter , The Lord of the Rings and The Matrix and is among the largest film studios in the world. The media company is also the owner of streaming service HBO Max and of series such as Game of Thrones . There must also be a committee that will supervise the editorial independence of news channels CBS News and CNN. The father of Paramount CEO David Ellison, Larry Ellison, maintains close ties with President Trump. The American president regularly expressed harsh criticism of CNN. He revoked CNN's press accreditation last month. That decision was reversed shortly afterwards by a judge. Cost savings The Ellisons did not let the grass grow under their feet. Today the company logo of Skydance appeared on the screens in CNN's headquarters in New York, writes The New York Times . A memo was also sent that pointed to possible cost savings. "The merger of two companies brings changes, including difficult decisions that affect our staff," wrote father and son. "We are determined to handle this process carefully and respectfully." Due to the merger, Skydance has a debt burden of around 80 billion dollars.

title: Cornell students furious about rape case: 'University afraid for reputation'
lead: In America, the protests are growing because of the rape case at the prestigious Cornell University. A student referred to as Jane Doe has filed a case because she says she was raped two years ago. Online, many women are expressing their anger with the hashtag #IAmJaneDoe, and yesterday around a thousand people held a protest march at the university in the state of New York. The alleged perpetrators of the rape, seven members of a student fraternity, were not punished or were only lightly punished by the university. The justice system will now investigate the case after all. But many Cornell students are also demanding action from the university. During yesterday's protest, the university administration building was slightly damaged. There were holes in one of the glass front doors and in red paint was written on the wall: "At Cornell, rapists are protected and protesters are sent away". Protest signs bore texts such as "Support victims, send rapists away", "Justice for every Jane Doe" and "Prison time, not punishment work". Student Lili-Rose Mas is taking part in the protest. She tells news agency Reuters: "It is very important that the people responsible feel the consequences. They should be in prison. And this is also a national issue, everyone thinks it is only Cornell, but it happens everywhere." Student Grace Xia agrees with her: "We think it is important to be here. Because if we don't make noise, we won't be seen, and then nothing changes. Then the board will just sweep this under the carpet again, and we want change." The demonstrators demand, among other things, an investigation into the way the university handled the rape case. They think the punishments are far too light: according to the complaint, some students involved only had to write an essay and had to be informed about sexual abuse and the use of social media. Cornell denies that writing an essay was the only punishment, but does not comment on the punishments for the individual suspects. Furthermore, the protesters demand that perpetrators of sexual violence are always punished to an equal degree. In the speeches during the demonstration, there is also criticism of Cornell's rector magnificus, Michael Kotlikoff. The university leadership would consider the institution's reputation more important than the students' safety. Some demonstrators demand the resignation of Kotlikoff and the board, because their policy would tolerate a "rape culture" at the university. Earlier research A study at Cornell University a few years ago revealed that one in three female students there has had unwanted sexual experiences. Newcomers warn each other about the dangers of parties at student fraternities. Nationwide, a quarter of female students in America have bad experiences. "Sexual violence happens far too often on campuses across the country," students write, for example, in the magazine of the University of Pennsylvania. According to The New York Times, between 2014 and 2019 there were around 6000 reports of rape at universities each year. During corona, that number decreased enormously because many campuses were closed at the time, but now it is increasing again. The student Jane Doe recently sued, among others, the university and the seven students. She says that under the influence of alcohol and drugs (ketamine) she had sex with the men. Because she was heavily under the influence, she could not defend herself. Otherwise, she says, she would certainly not have given consent. What exactly happened on that date, 19 October 2024, has not yet been clarified, The New York Times writes in a reconstruction . All seven men deny that they did anything wrong. Why the victim is called 'Jane Doe' In the American legal system, it is customary to call anonymous victims 'Jane Doe'. Men are called 'John Doe'. If there are more anonymous persons in one case, they are called 'Roe', as in the famous abortion case Roe v. Wade. Incidentally, in the Cornell University case, the victim's name would be circulating online. She is meanwhile being threatened , as are other women with the same name. The seven male suspects in this case are named with their full names in the American media.

title: Neder-Betuwe threatens fine for 24 rioters if things go wrong again
lead: <entity id="person:jan-kottelenberg">Burgemeester Kottelenberg</entity> of Neder-Betuwe wants to prevent the rioters who were involved in the anti-azc demonstrations in September from causing even more problems. He will therefore fine them in the event of a possible next demonstration that gets out of hand. It concerns 24 people. In a column on the municipality's website, Kottelenberg rejected the behavior of those involved. According to the mayor, four officers suffered hearing damage because rioters had thrown heavy fireworks. Demonstrators also smashed the windows of the town hall, insulted the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and did not follow the officers' orders. To prevent this, the mayor has now decided to impose a so-called order subject to a penalty payment. The 24 persons may no longer be involved in or present at disturbances during demonstrations anywhere in the municipality of Neder-Betuwe, reports Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> . If they do, they will receive a fine of at least 5000 euros and at most 15,000 euros per violation. The penalty payment applies for an indefinite period. Imposing an order subject to a penalty payment happens regularly with rioters, but much less often with demonstrators who are only present at riots. Both the police and a spokesperson for the municipality cannot, when asked, answer the question of whether the measure conflicts with the right to demonstrate. Not on the agenda A new demonstration against asylum reception has been announced for Thursday evening at the town hall in Opheusden in Neder-Betuwe. A college information evening will take place there then. Asylum reception is, incidentally, not on the agenda of that evening. The municipality expects that around a hundred young people will again turn up for the demonstration. The municipality has already made contact with the organizer of the protests, in the hope of making agreements. For example, the municipality wants to designate an area where demonstrators can stand.

title: Spy case damages reputation of German intelligence service
lead: "An absolute nightmare scenario," is how intelligence expert Kenneth Lasoen describes the news that the former head of the German foreign intelligence service has been detained. Lasoen is a professor of intelligence and security studies at the University of Antwerp. Former BND chief August Hanning (80) was arrested today on suspicion of treason and espionage. His close associate and confidant Manfred D., also chief of staff to Hanning's successor, was also detained. For which foreign service Hanning would have spied is not known. One of the few indications is a remark by a member of the German parliament. In a response to the arrests, that person said that working "for the enemies of liberal democracy" will not be tolerated. "But even then we still have a reasonably long list of countries," professor Lasoen tells NOS. Der Spiegel writes this evening that investigators assume Hanning was in contact with an agent of the secret service of Azerbaijan, but that has not been confirmed. 2000 documents Hanning was head of the BND from 1998 to 2005 and then state secretary of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> until the end of 2009. After that he continued as a private security adviser. The German Public Prosecution Service suspects that in the spring of 2010, thus after his time as BND chief and state secretary, he agreed with Manfred D. that the latter would provide him with valuable information from BND files in exchange for payment. According to the Public Prosecution Service, D. passed almost 2000 BND documents to Hanning up to June 2022, including a large number that were classified as "secret document" for internal use. In at least one case Hanning used documents to make an analysis for employees of a foreign security service, according to the Public Prosecution Service. What that analysis was about and whether it reached that service, the Public Prosecution Service does not yet know. Usual suspects The Süddeutsche Zeitung and the regional public broadcasters NDR and WDR conducted extensive research into the case. They were told that Hanning did not work for Russia. It would not surprise Kenneth Lasoen if it was China. "But it could just as well have been another country. The usual suspects are always Russia and China, but there are other services that make use of this kind of technique." Germany correspondent Chiem Balduk: "Even though the full extent is not yet clear, people in Germany are rightly speaking of a major scandal. The BND thrives on trust and needs it right now. The service wants more powers, to be better able to handle espionage and sabotage operations from Russia. Instead of only gathering information, the organisation must be reformed into a 'real' secret service that can also carry out missions abroad. A vote on that still has to be held in the Bundestag. This issue has not made that vote any easier. One can call for more powers, but this mainly raises the question of whether the service does not need more oversight." It is of course a disgrace for a security service when secrets are taken from under its fingers and passed to an enemy. "Then the first question is: what information has all been compromised?", says Lasoen. "Who has it and what impact has that had on German national security?" On top of that, the leaking of information endangers cooperation with friendly security services. "It does the reputation of the BND no good with its international partners when there is a chance that shared information ends up in the hands of hostile intelligence services. That can have quite a lot of consequences." By-catch What makes the case even more painful for the BND is that the suspicions against Hanning and his former chief of staff came to light by chance. The Public Prosecution Service in Hamburg was investigating a failed kidnapping of a child in 2022. This brought a security company with which Hanning worked into view. In September 2025 a raid followed on his home near Münster. The detectives took away crates full of documents. Analysing all that was in them took months. Only a few months ago was the BND informed of the discovery of the documents. In May of this year the national Public Prosecution Service took over the case from the colleagues in Hamburg.

title: House hopes to be able to deploy 130,000 citizens in crises
lead: The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> is charmed by the initiative to train citizens to be able to support the emergency services during disasters or crises. A majority today supported a motion by the CDA, in which the wish is expressed to have 130,000 of these so-called citizen reservists in four years. During a major crisis, the volunteers must prevent chaos from arising, especially in the first three days. <entity id="org:politie">Politie</entity>, army and emergency services cannot handle the work alone then, is the expectation. The reservists must be trained in three specialisms: technology, logistics and security. This concerns, for example, mechanics, drivers and security guards. They must form a kind of second shell around the armed forces. The initiative comes from BurgerReserve , which this year has already given about a thousand Dutch people a general skills training. The costs for this are paid by businesses and private individuals. In kind The House now wants <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to contribute to the expansion to 130,000 citizen reservists. Not with money, but in kind by making training grounds and teaching spaces of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> available free of charge. The cabinet has already said it shares the House's wish. What do such trainings look like? Nieuwsuur visited one: "The way we normally do things no longer works", director <entity id="person:karen-van-oudenhoven-van-der-zee">Karen van Oudenhoven-van der Zee</entity> of the <entity id="org:sociaal-en-cultureel-planbureau">Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau</entity> tells Nieuwsuur. Her organisation advocates increasing the resilience of citizens, so that crises can be absorbed better. As a possible crisis she mentions war, both in the Netherlands and elsewhere. Or the consequences of climate change, such as floods. "It may be that some products suddenly are no longer in the supermarket. Or there is a power outage or IT disruptions, so that transport is no longer possible." Catch-up After the Second World War, we in the Netherlands long had the idea that we had a grip on everything that could happen to us, says Van Oudenhoven. "The corona crisis was actually the first moment when we realised: something can happen just like that that makes us lose that grip. There is now more tension in the world than ever since the Second World War. In terms of resilience, we have a catch-up to make." As for national threat, the government has so far placed a great deal of emphasis on defence, she says. "What you see is that a great deal of attention goes to investments in weapons, in the army. And that there is relatively little attention for people and society. The budget in the Budget Memorandum for neighbourhoods and districts is 40 million. That is for 2027. After that it becomes 20 million for the two years after that. And if you then look at the investments in defence, that is not in proportion to each other."

title: British forensic student murders woman in 'Dexter' room
lead: In England, a forensic science student has confessed to murdering a 24-year-old woman, after luring her to a 'murder room' in an Airbnb property. Benjamin Day was obsessed with the television series Dexter, says the British public prosecutor. Last year in December, Day, then 19, called a sex worker with a disposable phone. He had rented a room in Tividale near Birmingham, which he had furnished based on a room from the American series. Dexter is about a forensic expert with the police who is also a serial killer and knows how to erase his traces. Shopping list Day lined the room with plastic wrap and made a "shopping list" that included an apron and cleaning products. He stabbed the woman 78 times and wanted to cut her into pieces, but stopped because he had injured himself. After the murder, the student left the property and called the emergency number to ask for medical help for himself. The police noticed that his story did not add up. Later, the landlord of the Airbnb also called the police, because another tenant had seen blood. After his arrest, Day initially said that he acted in self-defence and had only furnished the room to record a Dexter tribute for TikTok. Later he retracted that and, grinning, confessed guilt, writes the BBC. Day will hear on 4 December what his sentence will be. Earlier 'Dexter' murder It is not the first time that a Briton appears to have been inspired by the series to commit a murder. In 2014, a 17-year-old boy from England was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of his girlfriend, after he had stabbed her to death and sawed her into pieces in his bedroom.

title: Unrest in Hoogeveen for days, young people arrested again
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested six people in Hoogeveen this evening, including several minors. The centre has been restless for days: yesterday there were also eight arrests due to misconduct, such as throwing fireworks at passers-by. The police are emphatically present in the city centre. Because fireworks bangs were also heard this evening, officers frisked young people on the street, reports RTV <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity> . Minor young people In recent days incidents have regularly taken place in Hoogeveen. These often involve minor young people who, among other things, ride through the centre on fatbikes, intimidate passers-by and set off fireworks and throw them at people. The eight arrestees of yesterday evening were all minors. Furthermore, 32 fines were handed out and two fatbikes were confiscated. Earlier, the municipality tried to get the young people under control through the deployment of extra cameras and a gathering ban. The police will remain present in the centre this evening to prevent further escalation.

title: Christa Pike conscious and responsive after failed execution
lead: The prisoner from the American state of Tennessee who underwent a failed execution last week is conscious and responsive. Her lawyers have made this known. "Against all expectations, Christa Pike is conscious and can talk," the lawyers say in a statement after a visit to the hospital where Pike is staying. "She is still receiving intensive medical care. Despite the serious injuries to her arms, she is still chained to the bed with hand and foot shackles." The lawyers call her unexpected recovery "medically unprecedented". They expect it will take a long time before she is fully recovered. It is still unclear what will happen to her once she is back on her feet. Pricked twice The 50-year-old Pike had been sentenced to death because at age 18 she had tortured and murdered another teenager. Last Wednesday she was to become the first woman in 200 years to be executed in Tennessee, but that did not go according to plan. She received a dose of a substance that should have been deadly twice, but she kept breathing . After more than an hour the execution was halted and she was taken to the hospital. Pike's lawyers say that the executors of the execution had failed to find a vein, something they had warned about in advance. They suspect that the injection was misplaced, causing the deadly fluid not to enter her bloodstream. lead: Het kabinet wil de teruggang van het openbaar vervoer in regionale gebieden tegengaan door er steviger de controle over te nemen, zei staatssecretaris Anet Bertram van Infrastructuur in een

title: Much more went wrong in the monastery boarding schools, shows 'Meisjes van de Goede Herder: het vervolg'
Anyone who takes the professionalisation of teachers seriously stays away from the Promotiebeurs

lead: In 'Follow the Money interviewt' journalists Annette van Soest and Harm Ede Botje speak with key figures from various FTM dossiers. From supervisors and scientists to politicians and lawyers. Whether it concerns fraud and money laundering, our constitutional state or the future of our agricultural policy: Follow the Money interviewt.

title: Netherlands pulls out 'all the stops' to get Bolle Jos out of Sierra Leone
lead: Ending Europe's support for Sierra Leone is a concrete step to further increase pressure on the country to extradite criminal Jos Leijdekkers. "No diplomatic attempt has had any effect, so it is logical that the Netherlands looked for heavier means," says crime journalist for RTL Nieuws Koen Voskuil.

title: Acid rain from the eighties again a problem for dragonflies
lead: Typical dragonfly species of fens are declining sharply. The acid rain of some forty years ago is now causing very low oxygen levels in the water. Vroege Vogels visits the Deelense Was in Nationaal Park De Hoge Veluwe, a fen where this problem occurs.

title: 'Hackers could have shut down the power supply of hundreds of thousands of European households remotely'
lead: With a few quick actions, criminals or hostile states could possibly have shut down the power supply of hundreds of thousands of European households remotely. A Hague-based company revealed on Tuesday that it could access the control systems of more than 8500 wind and solar parks in 35 European countries via the internet. "With some I could even click the on and off button of a wind turbine."

title: Former German intelligence chief arrested on suspicion of espionage and treason
lead: The former head of the German intelligence service BND August Hanning has been detained. The German federal prosecutor has confirmed this after reporting by WDR, NDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung. Hanning is said to have been guilty of espionage.

title: Fernandes praises Ronaldo as symbol of Portuguese football
lead: PORTO (ANP/AFP) - Portugal international Bruno Fernandes has said that teammate Cristiano Ronaldo will forever be the greatest symbol of the Portuguese national team. The Manchester United footballer called for unity a day before the Nations League match against Norway, after tumultuous days following Ronaldo's walkout from the squad.

title: Amsterdam museums attract fewer visitors: 'Tourists are in the city for shorter periods and spend less money there'
Military aircraft with 32 passengers crashes in Nigeria: flags at half-mast throughout the country
lead: In Nigeria, a military aircraft with 32 occupants crashed yesterday. That happened in the southern state of Ondo. Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has declared three days of national mourning.

title: No hutspot from 1574, yet a Leiden classic
lead: Janneke Vreugdenhil does not have the recipe for 'the original Leiden hutspot from 1574', but she is happy to pass on the version she has been making in Leiden since her student days.

title: Scholen omringd door ongezond voedselaanbod; Gemeenten willen ingrijpen
lead: Een onderzoek van Amsterdam UMC in tien steden toonde aan dat bijna 94 procent van de middelbare en beroepsscholen omringd is door een overvloed aan ongezonde voedselopties.

title: Cabinet is favourably disposed towards a ban on slaughter without stunning
'With what I weighed then I could not win an Olympic medal. I was almost certain of that'
lead: As a judoka, Marit Kamps had successes in the so-called plus class (from 78 kilos). But against the very heavy women she could not compete. Now she is judoing her first World Championship in a lighter weight class. "I would never have been able to lift someone of 150 kilos."

title: Minister wil onderzoek naar boetes voor uitkeringsfraude bij niet-Nederlandse achternamen
lead: Mensen met een niet-Nederlandse achternaam krijgen vaker en harder een boete van de fraudedivisie van uitkeringsinstantie <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>, blijkt uit...

title: 25,000 old Lansingerland council documents remain offline
lead: Lansingerland previously took documents in the council information system (<entity id="org:rijksinkoopsamenwerking">RIS</entity>) offline after it emerged that personal data in them were unintentionally publicly accessible. The municipality reported the incident to the <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-persoonsgegevens">Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</entity> and announced in July that it was investigating the nature and scale of the data breach.

title: Many savers would not have been affected by cabinet plans for box 3
AEX closes at record high, bonds mark time
lead: The AEX closed at a record high. Elsewhere in Europe too the price boards turned green. The oil price fell to less than $100 per barrel of Brent and bonds marked time after a turbulent period.

Jetten keeps trying: 'step by step' without agreements
With a new way of testing you can free students from the current rat race

lead: Food security goes further than an emergency package for eight days. Look at the "talent" of an area, and adapt your production to it, says Jannemarie de Jonge. "More plant-based and fewer animals is a no brainer".

Paulien Cornelisse's legacy is anchored in the education of the future
The newest type of Russian kamikaze drone disrupts life in Kyiv: 'It comes and it brings death'
Why do we always want more?
lead: Do you recognise that? You have just bought something new and the next day you are already dissatisfied again. Or you treat yourself to that one piece of chocolate, but soon eat the whole bar. You are not the only one, but where does that greed come from and what can you do about it? "People need an environment in which you no longer receive certain stimuli," says Rutger Claassen, professor of Economic Ethics, on Spraakmakers.

title: ‘Never again Orbán!’: for a sovereign Europe, enlargement is needed, but under stricter conditions
Defence lets controversial arms dealer go his own way
lead: The boundary between Defence and the companies of arms dealer Martijn Walraven turns out to be blurred. Walraven and his consultant create the impression in business contacts that they are acting on behalf of the ministry. As a result, a navy ship that he bought from Defence stood parked free of charge for months on Defence grounds. Where does Defence stop and Walraven's private enterprise begin? Defence itself no longer seems to know.

title: Meeting the stem cell donor who saved your life? That may soon be possible
lead: You save someone's life, but you are then never allowed to meet that person. That is often the practice for stem cell donors. The <entity id="org:gezondheidsraad">Gezondheidsraad</entity> now advises allowing direct contact between stem cell donors and recipients, if they both want that.

title: Judge appears to back Booking in dispute over working from home with or
lead: Is it reasonable to oblige your staff to work in the office two days a week? The judge seemed inclined to side with Booking on this point.

title: Explosion in applications puts overfull power grid under pressure, but there is a bright spot
lead: The number of applications for power connections for new construction projects has exploded in the past six months. For the coming three years there are now 600,000 applications, more than twice as many as what is normally built in such a period. This keeps the pressure on the overfull power grid very high.

title: Former head of German intelligence service arrested for espionage and treason
Ambulance worker injured after collision while transporting patient with siren
lead: An ambulance worker was injured in a collision with a car in Rotterdam. The driver of the car was under the influence and did not have a driving licence. The ambulance was transporting a patient and was driving with siren and flashing lights on.

title: PSV player Ivan Perisic goes from hero to blunder with goal and red card in defeat against Spain
lead: No redemption for Croatia in Split. For a very long time the Croatians could hope for a draw against Spain, but in the closing stages Mikel Merino hurt the country: 1-2. Ivan Perisic played a leading role with a goal and a red card.

title: Van Bommel after 4-1 loss in France: 'A matter of time before we beat a top country'
lead: National coach Mark van Bommel of Belgium was remarkably positive after Monday's 4-1 defeat in the Nations League match against France. The Limburger thinks it is a matter of time before the 'Red Devils' beat a top country.

title: Government teleworking system possibly hacked: 'Vigilance required'
lead: The Rijksoverheid takes into account that hackers have penetrated Citrix. Citrix is used by the government to give employees remote access to the systems. Hospitals also use it. Multiple government organisations are being investigated for possible traces of a break-in. That is what state secretary <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> writes in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Cornell students protest against handling of rape case
lead: Students of Cornell University have protested to express support for the victim of the 2024 rape case. The young woman and her lawyer reported that they have received multiple threats after filing the lawsuit. The students are angry about how <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the judiciary have handled the case.

title: From Thatcher's confidant to prisoner: Jeffrey Archer's life (1940-2026) was one long string of controversies

lead: The talents of status holders, asylum seekers and Ukrainian displaced persons are insufficiently used in the Netherlands. According to a new advisory report from the Sociaal-Economische Raad (SER), these newcomers should be helped into work better, for example in sectors with staff shortages.

title: Democracy is stronger than it looks
lead: Open societies have weathered murderous leftists and fascist radicals before.

title: Cabinet will spare small savers and investors after all, plans adjusted again
lead: The cabinet wants to prevent an additional 850,000 savers and investors from having to pay tax on their assets after all. Minister <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> (VVD, <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) is going to adjust his plans again, now that he is receiving fierce criticism in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>.

title: Dutch former Flydubai pilot: 'Knife in cockpit is almost unthinkable'
lead: A stabbing in the cockpit caused a scheduled flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv to make an emergency landing this week. For that, the aircraft descended several kilometers in a short time. A crash was prevented by intervention of passengers. But how can something like that happen in one of the most strictly secured environments in the world? And above all: how does a sharp object get into the cockpit?

title: VVD voter drops out after shuffling with budget plans: well over half more negative about cabinet
lead: The cabinet changed its budget plans this week, immediately received sharp criticism for it and reversed part of it barely two days later. Especially VVD voters are unhappy with all the unrest: 55 percent of them have started thinking more negatively about the cabinet in recent days. This is evident from research by the RTL Nieuwspanel among more than 18,000 participants.

title: What will the massacre of 7 October be called in the history books?
Van 't Schip loses with Kazakhstan also to Moldova
lead: John van 't Schip also failed to win the third match as national coach of Kazakhstan. In its own Astana, the team lost 2-1 to Moldova.

title: Remote house in Iceland finally self-sufficient after 70 years
lead: On the remote island of Elliðaey near Iceland stands a house that was dependent on fuel and propane for years. Thanks to new solar panels, the old hunters' cabin is now self-sufficient and much easier to use for hunters and tourists.

title: This ice scene from 1625 (worth 11 million euros) shows how skilled the painter Hendrick Avercamp was
A cover letter with your bid? Sellers at Amsterdam’s Open House Day don’t even read them: ‘It’s about the best price’
Public Prosecution Service will from now on always demand prison sentence after physical violence against emergency workers
lead: Anyone who uses physical violence against emergency workers and officials with a public task must seriously expect a prison sentence. The Public Prosecution Service must in principle always demand that sentence. This is stated in a new guideline, which comes after a majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> had urged this.

title: Messi says farewell to Argentina: 'The moment has come'
lead: "The moment has come. I leave in peace. I have given everything." This is how Lionel Messi begins his farewell message ahead of his last match for Argentina. The 39-year-old forward plays tonight in the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires against Benin. The match is entirely dominated by his farewell to the national team.

title: Jong Oranje to play-offs for European Championship at the last moment through win over Bosnia and help from Norwegians
lead: Jong Oranje reached the play-offs for European Championship qualification on Tuesday. The team of national coach Michael Reiziger beat Bosnia and Herzegovina in Doetinchem 4-0, while rival Israel drew against Norway.

title: As a witness to the Holocaust, Irene Butter (1930-2026) ultimately felt responsible for telling about it
Plane collides with zebra during take-off and makes belly landing in Tanzania
lead: A plane with thirty people made an emergency landing in Tanzania, after it collided with a zebra during take-off. The impact with the animal damaged the landing gear. The aircraft ultimately had to land without working landing gear and slid on its belly along the runway.

title: Trump does everything for the image
Conifers make way for deciduous trees to curb wildfires
lead: In Dutch forests, conifers are being replaced by deciduous trees in some places to reduce the risk of wildfires. Deciduous trees catch fire less quickly. The adjustment must also ensure that people can leave the area more safely in the event of a large fire.

title: Policy for participation of trans persons in amateur sport 'discriminatory'
lead: At at least six sports federations, trans and non-binary amateur athletes must apply for an exemption or undergo a medical examination in order to take part in competitions. That policy is discriminatory, concludes the National Coordinator against Discrimination and Racism (NCDR) Rabin Baldewsingh.

title: Members of Kazakhstan's military leadership arrested after death of 14 servicemen
lead: Five members of the military leadership in Kazakhstan have been arrested after fourteen servicemen died during an exercise. The servicemen had ended up in the water during a mission on a boat. The president speaks of "criminal unprofessionalism".

title: Data Protection Officers experience less support within the organisation
lead: Data Protection Officers (DPOs) in the public sector are increasingly dealing with new issues around algorithms and digital innovation. While available time, support and budgets are under pressure. This is evident from the DPO survey 2026 by Centrum Informatiebeveiliging en Privacybescherming (CIP).

title: Toddler pulls out loaded pistol at daycare centre in US
lead: A 3-year-old toddler pulled out his mother's loaded pistol at a daycare centre in the US state of Michigan. There, the weapon, which was in a holster, was passed to other children. An employee saw it happen and intervened. No one was injured.

title: Groningen BBB wants to talk with coalition after motion of no confidence
lead: The Groningen BBB faction hopes to hear from coalition partners PvdA, GroenLinks and VVD this week how they want to proceed within the provincial government. PvdA, GroenLinks and VVD supported a motion of no confidence against the BBB, by far the largest coalition faction, in the Provincial Council last Wednesday. "That has not left us unmoved," said BBB leader Bas Wiegmans on Monday evening after consultation with his faction. Party leader Henk Vermeer was also present.

title: Leiden breaks The Hague formation record
lead: The <entity id="org:gemeenteraad-leiden">gemeenteraad van Leiden</entity> concludes the formation period of a new coalition and executive on Thursday with the appointment of seven aldermen. Leiden thereby arrives at a formation period of 197 days and breaks the formation record of the major cities.

title: Jetten: 'Confidence that we can get the million note across the finish line'
lead: The planned billions in cuts to the unemployment benefit (WW) and the disability benefit (WIA) are completely off the table. It is one of the points in the adjusted budget proposal that was sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> on Tuesday. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> still hopes for broad support in the Kamer for the entire million note. To achieve that, the cabinet says it is prepared to enter into discussions with the opposition on a further series of subjects during the budget debates.

title: A grown-up coat for Konijnenvoer in Arnhem
lead: Restaurant Konijnenvoer has known various forms, but the newest incarnation is of a different caliber, writes Joël Broekaert . The amuses set the tone: elegant, local, plant-based, creative and flavorful.

title: Man (20) from Purmerend forced girl (16) to cut herself and carve 'Zoro' into her skin
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> suspects 20-year-old Mohammed H. from Purmerend of mistreating a 16-year-old girl in Rotterdam by pressuring her online and instructing her to cut herself. According to the OM, the victim had to carve the name Zoro into her body with a sharp object between 30 April and 10 July, causing her to sustain scars.

title: Tennis player Sinner also misses tournament in Shanghai due to knee injury
lead: Tennis player Jannik Sinner also misses the Masters tournament in Shanghai that starts next week. The five-time Grand Slam champion has not yet recovered enough from the knee injury that has kept him sidelined since his title at Wimbledon. Sinner (25) had planned to return this week in the Chinese Beijing, but earlier also withdrew for that.

title: New NAM director actually finds dismantling gas installations 'terrible'
lead: Martijn Kleverlaan starts on 1 November as head of NAM, the oil and gas company that has shrunk enormously in recent years.

title: At the press conference jaws drop: Dani Olmo turns out to have been giving money for years to a city full of war wounds
lead: Spain closes the international period tonight with an away match against Croatia. For Spanish international Dani Olmo that is a very special fixture. In Croatia he took the first big step in his career as a 16-year-old boy. Out of gratitude he supports the country in a special way and that earned him loud applause during the press conference.

title: Belgium and Van Bommel heavily beaten at France after four late goals from substitutes
lead: Belgium was unable to pull off an upset at France in the Nations League on Monday. The team of national coach Mark van Bommel led 0-1 in Paris for a long time, but conceded four goals from substitutes in the closing stages: 4-1.

title: Total ban on mobile phones at school also has a downside: 'If parents relax at home, you achieve nothing'
lead: From 1 January, mobile phones will also be banned in the schoolyard and during breaks. That is at least the tightened cabinet advice for primary and secondary schools. Sounds logical, but it can also go too fast, experts warn. "Lonely children can become even more isolated."

title: Women footballers Ajax and PSV win away matches in Eredivisie
lead: The women footballers of Ajax and PSV recorded victories in away matches in the Women's Eredivisie on Sunday. Ajax beat Feyenoord in Rotterdam 4-1. PSV won 3-0 on visit to ADO Den Haag.

title: The Netherlands has become a reading-unfriendly society
Djokovic reaches semi-final in Beijing after win over Zverev
lead: Tennis player Novak Djokovic (39) has reached the semi-final at the China Open at the expense of Alexander Zverev. The Serbian 24-time Grand Slam winner thereby remains unbeaten in Beijing, he won the tournament in all six of his previous appearances. He defeated the German number 2 of the world in three sets: 4-6 6-4 6-4.

title: School strike in France escalates: principal doused in gasoline, schools set on fire
lead: What began as a protest against overcrowded classes and poorly maintained school buildings has grown into a nationwide popular protest in France. Students from hundreds of schools have been on 'strike' for days and are becoming more and more violent. Today a school principal was doused in gasoline and fires were set at two schools.

title: Smaller savers spared after pressure from the House: 'We are not going to do that'
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is reversing the plan to make savers and investors pay capital gains tax sooner. The cabinet wanted to use the extra tax revenues to pay for a repair to box 3. How the cabinet will now pay for that is still unknown.

title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal squad a day before duel with Denmark
lead: Star player Cristiano Ronaldo has left the training camp of the Portuguese team a day before the Nations League match against Denmark. The 41-year-old footballer did so after statements by national coach Jorge Jesus at the press conference, who earlier said that nothing was wrong.

title: Oranje salvages a point in Greece after weak first half
lead: The Dutch national team has narrowly avoided a first defeat under head coach Xavi Hernández. The away match against Greece ended 2-2 in Thessaloniki. At halftime, Oranje was still trailing 2-0.

title: Discontent in Japan grows after arrest of American serviceman for murder of woman
lead: Among the Japanese population, discontent is growing about the presence of American servicemen after one of them was arrested for the murder of a woman. Protests are being held on the southern island group of Okinawa.

title: German footballers give Klopp first win against Serbia
lead: Germany has secured its first win under head coach Jürgen Klopp. The Germans won 2-0 against Serbia in Munich in the Nations League.

title: Cabinet wants to protect children better online, including by keeping phones out of school
lead: The cabinet presents a strategy letter for online children's rights on Monday. Several ministries are working together on these measures. The cabinet believes that some digital services are still "too unsafe" for children.

title: Former football director Nijland advisor at skating team Team X2O
lead: Hans Nijland, former director of FC Groningen, is going to work in the skating world. The 66-year-old football administrator becomes commercial advisor at Team X2O Badkamers, which was still called Team IKO-X2O last season. He must, among other things, help the team with attracting new sponsors.

title: Can AI exterminate humanity for paperclips? Makers think so
lead: The warnings are not mild. Artificial intelligence poses an 'existential threat' to humanity, AI company Anthropic says in its own stock prospectus. But what is so dangerous about AI? To explain that, some experts use a metaphor with paperclips.

title: Death from poisonous mushroom: this is how you recognise it
lead: It grows normally in Dutch forests, but is considered the deadliest mushroom in the world: the death cap. This year, seven people have already received a special antidote after serious poisoning. One person died. In this video we show how to recognise it.

title: Ceciel from B&B vol liefde wants media to be more critical of Fred: 'He was sometimes transgressive'
lead: The media are not critical enough of Fred's 'transgressive' behavior during B&B vol liefde, participant Ceciel believes. She finds it painful that the controversial B&B owner is portrayed as a hero. "He has hurt people," she tells this site.

title: According to the neighbours, this house must be demolished: it stands too close to the road
lead: A home in Kesteren in Gelderland must be moved almost 2 metres back because the neighbours think the house stands too far forward.

title: 'Dutchman appointed minister in controversial Sudan government'
lead: A man from the Netherlands was appointed early May as Minister of Justice in a controversial government of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan. That is reported by <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity> based on its own research.

title: Closing Time | Dirty Three
lead: Dirty Three is the band of Warren Ellis, who is mainly known as a Bad Seed. More than an ordinary Bad Seed even, because Nick Cave has undertaken very little for years without working intensively with Ellis. With Nick Cave he is in the service of music, which over time […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: How municipalities struggle with online council information
lead: The scale of the problems that municipalities experience with leaked personal data in council documents differs considerably. In <entity id="org:gemeente-zuidplas">Zuidplas</entity> almost the entire council information system was recently withdrawn from public access and part of the historical archive will not return directly. <entity id="org:gemeente-pijnacker-nootdorp">Pijnacker-Nootdorp</entity> spent 16,000 euros on the checks after which 35 documents went offline. <entity id="org:gemeente-voorschoten">Voorschoten</entity> did this for only one document.

title: Flydubai lost altitude of 13 Eiffel Towers in one minute: 'You normally never see this'
lead: The Flydubai aircraft that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia today made an enormous dive in a short time. This appears from data from Flightradar. In less than a minute the plane lost 4 kilometers of altitude, roughly equal to 23 Euromasts stacked on top of each other, or 13 Eiffel Towers. "That must have hurt the ears considerably," says aviation expert Joris Melkert.

title: Netanyahu seeks gain in near-plane disaster
lead: A near-disaster with a radical co-pilot could help Benjamin Netanyahu in the run-up to the elections. But the same flight could also expose where his security state has failed.

title: Thanks to a new operation, Herma can enjoy sex again after vulvar cancer
lead: When Herma heard that she had vulvar cancer, she thought intimacy would be over forever. Thanks to a new surgical technique, she can enjoy sex again. The treatment is now also being taught to other doctors.

title: Frank Houtappels on film Downtown and AIDS epidemic: 'I had completely repressed it'
lead: Writer and actor Frank Houtappels, known from among others Gooische Vrouwen, returns with Downtown to one of the most important themes in his oeuvre: friendship. The film is set in the 1980s and follows three friends who throw themselves into Amsterdam's nightlife with abandon, until the AIDS epidemic changes everything. In Kunststof, Houtappels talks about stage fright, his personal inspiration behind the new film and AIDS.

Norwegian skater died who benefited from legendary mistake by Van der Duim

lead: With a renovation costing more than 80 million euros, the Formula 1 team of Mercedes AMG-Petronas is building a hypermodern headquarters in Brackley. Reporter Tim Hartman got an exclusive look behind the doors that opened for once for 'peeping toms'. "Here our world titles are won."

title: Three weeks after the disaster, hope of survivors in the Nepalese mud has vanished
lead: More than three weeks after a churning torrent of water, mud and debris raced through Nepal, hope is evaporating that survivors will still be found in the disaster area, which is covered with a thick layer of silt. In the damaged homes, personal belongings left behind bear witness to the lives destroyed by the disaster.

lead: A cold front leaves our country today via the east. Especially there it is cloudy for a large part of the day and showers can still fall occasionally. The rest of the country has sun, clouds and a local shower.

lead: It is to be the final piece of the party merger: a referendum on the question of which group PRO will join in the European Parliament after the 2029 elections. Members must declare their party colour, while that discussion has so far remained in the background.

title: Seven times Paulien Cornelisse at her sharpest: 'What makes people different from animals is that they want to improve each other'
lead: Making the small big and the big small. Writer, cabaret artist and programme maker Paulien Cornelisse could do it like no one else. Seven highlights from the NRC archive.

title: The beauty of a photo of Afghan children briefly distracts from why they are walking here

lead: A school in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv has been hit by a Russian drone. During the attack, children were in the shelter, no one was injured. An important bridge in the city was also hit.

title: Asylum children exposed to unsafe living conditions
lead: Children in asylum emergency shelter are now structurally 'exposed to unsafe living conditions that pose serious risks to their development', writes the <entity id="org:zbo-onderzoeksraad-voor-veiligheid">Onderzoeksraad voor Veiligheid</entity> (OVV) in the report 'Kinderen in nood' published on Monday. title: Daniil Medvedev loses nearly 200,000 euros in prize money and hope of ATP points after hitting ball at spectator

lead: Where you live determines how well you are protected against high healthcare costs. Some 160,000 people currently have no municipal policy because the municipality does not offer one or contributes too little to the premium, according to research by the independent think tank Instituut voor Publieke Economie (IPE). lead: France has carried out a test with a new nuclear missile. President Emmanuel Macron shared images of the launch on social media. 'To be free, you must be feared. And to be feared, you must be powerful', he wrote in unmistakable terms.

title: Video | Parents and unions join student protest in France
Trump approves execution by firing squad of man who killed 13 service members

lead: French school students are blocking access to their schools in protest against overcrowded classrooms, long days, a shortage of teachers and dirty, overheated school buildings. lead: More and more tankers and cargo ships sail under the flag of marginal flag states, because they have flexible rules. The Dutch company Dutch Lloyd cleverly responds to this and arranges the flags of Cameroon, Mongolia and Somalia, among others. FTM spoke with the owner.

title: Strangely enough
lead: In our little frog country we are quite bad at making room in a somewhat practical way for 'feelings', certainly the negative ones. Fear, sadness, anger, mourning, shame and also desire and ambition, what the ancient Greeks call pathos. We joke pain away or declare fear and anger outside the prevailing order. We mourn for a month at most. And we quickly paper over value conflicts with some technocracy, a convenient majority and a thick layer of legalism.

lead: Every six months the clock is changed by an hour, but why do we actually do that? Is it good for us? And a few handy tips, so you never again forget whether the clock should be set forward or back.

title: Belgian farmer guilty of murder of daughters, hears sentence today

The minister said this on Sunday in Buitenhof . People are entitled to money if the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity> takes too long over their application, but due to major backlogs Vijlbrief wanted to temporarily do away with the administrative fines.

title: Former holiday parks of Peter Gillis go to the highest bidders: creditor agrees to 27.3 million

title: Former AIVD chief Bertholee warns: Netherlands not yet ready for Russian threat
lead: The Netherlands is not yet sufficiently prepared for the increasing threat from Russia. lead: LISBON (ANP/RTR) - The whistleblower behind Football Leaks, whose revelations helped lead to the investigation into Manchester City's financial malpractice, will very soon lose his witness protection. According to his legal team, the situation of the Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto is 'critical', because in a few days he must leave his protected home address without any guarantee of police protection. "His situation is now critical. The threats against him are not merely theoretical; he was attacked in Lisbon last April."

title: Foam shows the beautiful photos of Chinese rising star Hailun Ma - but what exactly are we looking at?
lead: The Chinese fashion photographer Hailun Ma is one of the emerging talents of her country. For the photos in Hometown, her first major solo outside China, she returned to her native region of Xinjiang. Should the Amsterdam photography museum Foam have provided more context?

The <entity id="org:inspectie-gezondheidszorg-en-jeugd">Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd</entity> (IGJ) has stopped the production of the required study medication, according to Amsterdam 'unexpectedly and for reasons unclear to us'.

title: Greece and Germany draw, Oranje to first place
lead: Greece and Germany drew on Sunday evening in the Nations League. In Thessaloniki it became 0-0. Due to that result, Oranje, which won 2-1 against Serbia, takes the lead in group 2 of the A division from the Greeks. The Netherlands and Greece both have 8 points, an equal head-to-head result and the same goal difference. Oranje leads on the basis of the number of goals scored. Germany is third with 5 points.

title: This bodycheck broke the entire Dutch hockey team: on the aftermath of a painful World Cup

Minister is fed up with dubious role of estate agents and intervenes
lead: Stricter rules for estate agents are coming to tackle the abuses in that sector. That is announced today by Minister Elanor Boekholt-O'Sullivan (D66) of Housing. In the most extreme case, an estate agent can even receive a work ban.

title: Female top chef also loses her second Michelin star: 'Unexpected and bewildering'
lead: The Limburg chef Margo Reuten, one of the few female top chefs in our country, has also lost her last star. Michelin informed her of this yesterday morning, a day before the presentation of the new guide. "An unexpected and bewildering message", Reuten calls the loss of the star for her restaurant Da Vinci in Maasbracht.

title: Cabinet has a new offer for the opposition and wants to improve purchasing power in it
lead: The cabinet made a new offer to the opposition on Tuesday. The cuts to social security are off the table and a new plan for box 3 is paid for by tinkering with tax rules. The cabinet also wants to improve purchasing power for working people.

title: Portuguese football association wants solution for 'misunderstanding' about Ronaldo
lead: Chairman Pedro Proença of the Portuguese football association wants the row about Cristiano Ronaldo in the Portuguese national team to be resolved. According to the chairman, the whole matter is based on a misunderstanding and the bond with the star is close.

title: Rob lost his dog and could not work: getting time off is then not self-evident
lead: The 51-year-old Rob Steenvoorde from Leiden knows how hard the loss of a pet can hit. But where you are often entitled to leave when a family member dies, there is almost nothing arranged for a deceased pet. "If you say that I have to come to work, then expect a crying guy at the office."

title: Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Belgian physicist Francis Halzen, who caught 'ghostly' particles in the ice of Antarctica

title: The month of September in Pictures
lead: Every day thousands of photos from around the world flow into our image banks. From gruesome current events to tranquil landscapes, from breaking news to seemingly small moments. Every month the photo editors of NRC select the photos that made the most impression.

title: Why astrophysicist Heino Falcke sees precisely in the big bang an indication for the existence of God
lead: Science and faith have been an exciting combination for centuries. Can you believe in God, if science cannot prove his existence? Yes, that is perfectly possible, says astrophysicist Heino Falcke in De Ongelooflijke Podcast (EO). He recently wrote a book about the history of our planet. Precisely in the big bang he sees the hand of God.
