title: Eye injury from padel occurs often: 'The eye can even tear'
lead: Ophthalmologists see padel players with serious eye injuries several times a week after they got a ball in their eye. That is why they are raising the alarm and advocating for safety glasses on the padel court.

title: Health Council: allow personal contact in stem cell donation
lead: No more anonymous letters, but a personal thank-you: as far as the Health Council is concerned, stem cell patients and donors may from now on exchange personal contact details with each other.

title: France and Germany ask the European Commission to act more strictly against China, without naming the country
lead: European industry is groaning under competition from Chinese companies, which benefit among other things from government subsidies and a favourable exchange rate. France and Germany want Europe to have an effective trade weapon ready against unfair trade practices.

title: Amazon Kroeze wins first national eventing title in Boekelo
lead: Renske Kroeze has won the Dutch eventing championship for the first time at the Military Boekelo-Enschede. The 37-year-old amazon kept three-time Dutch champion Janneke Boonzaaijer behind her in the all-round discipline in equestrian sport.

title: Union: violence on trains is getting worse, more boa's needed
lead: The union for railway personnel VVMC is raising the alarm about the growing number of violent incidents on the railways. The union has sent an urgent letter to politicians. According to the union, the number of incidents and their severity increases every year.

title: OM will demand higher sentences for violence against police officers and other emergency workers
lead: Anyone who assaults a police officer, ambulance worker or someone else with a public task can count on a considerably higher sentencing demand. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has made new agreements about this with the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the OM.

title: WHO sees no plague infections in deceased laboratory technician
lead: The World Health Organization says Russia has completed the contact investigation following the death of an employee of an anti-plague institute. There was fear that the laboratory technician had died from the consequences of the infectious disease.

title: Judge remands Turkish referees boss in custody on corruption charges
lead: ISTANBUL (ANP/AFP) - The head of the Turkish referees organization has been taken into provisional custody by the court. Ferhat Gündoğdu is said to have been guilty of manipulating, among other things, appointments and nominations of referees. His arrest is also connected to the large-scale betting scandal in the Turkish refereeing world. A year ago, the football association suspended 149 referees on suspicion of illegal betting on matches.

title: Kenniscentrum Europa Decentraal to VNG
lead: As of 1 January 2027, Kenniscentrum Europa Decentraal (KED) will transfer to the Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten (VNG). The KED, which will exist for 25 years next year, was always an independent foundation. The goal remains unchanged: the KED translates European law and policy into the practice of all decentralised authorities.

title: What travel expenses do MEPs declare? You can only see it once they have been convicted
lead: The European Parliament normally does not want to give insight into the travel expense declarations of parliamentarians. But it does now that Follow the Money asked for information about the British former parliamentarian Nathan Gill. The reason: Gill is a convicted criminal.

title: Criminals take over homes of vulnerable people
lead: More than 50 municipalities are dealing with criminals who misuse the homes of vulnerable people for drug crime. Housing corporations are very concerned about this development. More and more vulnerable people live in social rental homes, and so the risk of criminal exploitation rises, according to municipalities, <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and housing corporations.

title: Verstappen wants to win at least once this season
lead: Max Verstappen wants to win at least one race this season in Formula 1. The four-time world champion said this at the FIA press conference ahead of the postponed Bahrain Grand Prix, which will be held in Malaysia this weekend. "I have now regularly stood on the podium, but I want to win. That is why I am in this sport," said the driver of Red Bull, who turned 29 on Wednesday.

title: Nasreddine has been living on the beach in Ceuta for two months now. 'Life is hard here, but I really don't want to go back to Morocco'
lead: The Spanish authorities are increasing the pressure on the remaining migrants in Ceuta, including by clearing a tent camp. With small trading and by taking on odd jobs, the migrants try to survive. "They say there is no place for us in Europe."

title: Jacky (46) no longer wants to be ashamed of her face: 'I am still here, so let me show myself'
lead: Jacky Ghijsen (46) had cancer several times as a child, teenager and adult and was told she would not live long. But she is still here. After the treatments she lost an eye, upper jaw, palate and teeth. She was ashamed of the severe scars on her face, but she has put that behind her. "I am still here. Why should I not show myself then?"

title: Former German spy chief arrested for treason and espionage
lead: The former German chief of the intelligence service August Hanning was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of espionage and treason. The eighty-year-old Hanning was head of intelligence service BND from 1998 to 2005.

title: Le Monde: FIFA let ineligible Congolese play at World Cup
lead: World football association FIFA would have let a player from Congo play at the World Cup and in qualifying matches, while he was not eligible to play. Le Monde reported this on Tuesday based on documents reviewed by the French newspaper. It would concern goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi (32), who has played in French youth teams. Mpasi would never have fully completed the process of switching from France to Congo, which would have made him ineligible to play for Congo.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu speaks of a 'period for internal democracy'.

title: Longer working by early retirees only limitedly reduces teacher shortage
lead: Working longer can only limitedly reduce the staff shortages in primary and secondary education. If all teachers who retired at least one school year before the state pension age had continued working one year longer, that would on average have yielded approximately 770 fte extra in primary education (po) and 520 fte in secondary education (vo).

title: Former head of German intelligence service BND arrested on suspicion of espionage and attempted treason
lead: August Hanning left the BND in 2005, but is said to have secret BND documents, some of which date from 2022. At least once he is said to have made a security analysis for a foreign intelligence service.

title: Conviction of main character in documentary Verstoten vaders shows how complex it is to tackle intimate terrorism

title: What does scaling up do to local tourism?
lead: The family of journalist and radio maker Jozien Wijkhuijs has had a beach house on the coast of Walcheren since her childhood. Every summer they holiday there for weeks, they know the place and the people inside out. Now that her father is getting older and fears that large holiday parks are advancing all the way to the beach, Wijkhuijs, her brothers and sister face a choice; invest in maintenance and keep the cottage in the family for as long as possible, or sell now that the cottage can still yield a substantial amount? Jozien explores that question in the DOCS audio documentary Ons strandhuis.
